stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Ada

axes.where: on a roof across the town

stories.text:
When Ada got a new hat for her doll, she clapped her hands. The hat was small and blue. It had a tiny red flower on the side.

Ada put the hat on her doll. The doll looked happy. Ada said, "You are so pretty."

Her friend Ben came over. He said, "I like the hat. Let's have a tea party."

They sat on the porch. Ada brought a jar of water. Ben gave a soft tap to the little cup. The doll sat with them.

Then Ada saw something far away. On a roof across the town, a little light shone. It was green. It made her feel calm and quiet. She looked at it for a while.

"Ada," said Ben. "More tea?"

Ada turned back. "Yes," she said. She did not need to go to that roof. Her doll was here. The light was just a light.

They played until the sun went down. The little green light blinked on the roof, but Ada was happy with her hat and her friend.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Ada

axes.where: on a roof across the town

stories.text:
When Ada got a new hat for her doll, she clapped. The hat was small and blue. It had a tiny flower on the side. Ada put it on her doll. The doll looked happy. Ada smiled.

Her friend Ben came over. “Let’s play outside,” he said. Ada put the doll in her bag. She kept the hat in a jar so it would not get lost. They went out into the sunny afternoon.

Ben ran to the fence. Ada sat on the grass. She took the hat from the jar and put it on the doll again. The sun was warm. It felt calm.

Then Ada saw something far away. On a roof across the town, a little light shone. It was small and green. It looked like a tiny leaf that would not fall. Ada did not know why, but she wanted to touch it.

“What do you see?” Ben asked.

“That light,” Ada said. “It is so far.”

Ben did not laugh. He gave her a soft tap on the arm. “We can look at it together,” he said. So they did. The doll wore her hat. Ada held the jar. The green light stayed far away, but Ben stayed close.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Ada

axes.where: on a roof across the town

stories.text:
When Ada got a new hat for her doll, she clapped. The hat was small and blue. It had a tiny bow. Ada put it on her doll. The doll looked happy.

Ada went outside. The sun was warm. She saw a little light on a roof across the town. It was green and soft. It did not move. Ada wanted to touch it. She did not know how.

Her friend Ben came by. "Why do you look sad?" he said. Ada said, "I want that light." Ben said, "That is far away." Ada said, "I want it still."

They sat on a step. Ben gave her a jar. "Put your calm inside," he said. Ada held the jar. She did a tap, tap, tap on the lid. The light stayed on the roof.

Ada put the doll's hat in the jar. The light was still there. She looked and looked. Ben said, "Let's play." Ada said, "I want that light." She said it again. "I want that light." The sun went down. The light did not come to her.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Ada

axes.where: on a roof across the town

stories.text:
When Ada got a new hat for her doll, she smiled. The hat was small and red. It had a tiny flower on the side. Ada put it on her doll. "You look pretty," she said.

Then she saw the light. It was far away, on a roof across the town. It was small and green. It did not move. Ada wanted to touch it.

Her friend Ben came over. "Let's play," he said.

"I want that light," Ada said. She put her doll down. She forgot the hat.

Ben gave her a jar. "We can catch it," he said.

Ada held the jar up. She tried to tap the light with her finger. It was too far. The afternoon was sunny and warm. Ada felt calm for a little bit. Then she looked at the roof again.

"I want it," she said. "I want it. I want it."

Ben sat with her. He did not laugh. He said, "The light is pretty. Your doll's hat is pretty too."

Ada looked at her doll. The red hat was still there. She held her doll close. The light stayed on the roof. Ada said, "I want it," one more time. Then she put the hat back on her doll.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Ada

axes.where: on a roof across the town

stories.text:
When Ada got a new hat for her doll, she put it on right away. The hat was small and blue. Her friend Ben came to see.

"Look," said Ada. "My doll has a hat."

Ben smiled. "It is pretty."

Then Ada saw it. On a roof across the town, a little light was shining. It was green and small. The sun was bright, but the light did not go away.

"I want to go there," said Ada.

She put her doll in a jar to keep it safe. Ben said, "We can tap on the roof."

"No," said Ada. "I want the light. I want the light."

Ben held her hand. "Stay calm. We can look from here."

But Ada did not want to look. She wanted to touch it. She wanted the light. She wanted the light. The doll's hat fell down. Ada did not see it. She only saw the small green light on the roof across the town.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Faye

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
A doll named Faye got a new hat. It was red with a wide brim. The wind blew hard that morning. Faye held the hat with both hands.

She took the hat to the playground. She put it on the drum and gave it a bounce. The hat flew up, then landed on a dog. The dog ran. Faye ran too. A funny moment! The dog shook. The hat fell in a puddle.

Faye sat on a swing. The wind grew calm. She looked far across the playground. A little light was on, small and warm, near the fence. She wanted to walk to it. She did not know why. She watched it blink. Then she went home.

Her hat was wet and bent. Mother put it on a shelf. Faye could not wear it again. That night she thought of the small light. It stayed far away. She felt sad.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Faye

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
A doll and her new hat were ready. Faye put the hat on her doll. The wind blew and the hat went up. It went over the fence.

Faye ran to get it. The wind took it to the far side of the playground. She saw a small light there. It was green and quiet. It did not move.

The hat landed on a drum. A boy hit the drum. Boom, boom. The hat bounced up and down. Faye laughed. That was funny.

She got her hat back. She put it on the doll. The wind blew again. The hat flew away. It went high and far. Faye looked at the green light. It was still there. It was calm. She could not reach it. She held her doll tight. The doll had no hat now. Faye felt sad.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Faye

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
A doll needs a hat on a windy morning. Faye made one from a leaf and a bit of string. She put it on her doll. The wind said whoosh. The hat flew off and did a funny dance in the air.

Faye laughed. Then she ran to get it. The wind pushed it along like a little drum. She had to bounce over a puddle. She caught the hat near the fence.

Far away, across the playground, a light shone. It was small and far. It sat on a pole and did not move. Faye looked at it. She wanted to touch it. She held her doll and looked and looked. The light was too far. It was always too far.

She put the hat back on her doll. The wind took it again. This time it went up high. It went over the fence. It landed in the road. Faye could not go there.

She sat down. The wind made her calm. But her doll had no hat. And the far light still shone.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Faye

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
A doll sat on the bench. Faye made her a hat from a red leaf. The wind blew hard. The hat went up, up, and away.

Faye ran. She did not see the puddle. Splash! Her shoes got wet. She did not care. She wanted the hat.

Then she stopped. On the far side of the playground, past the slide, a small light shone. It was soft and green. It sat on the fence post. It said, Come here. Come here. Faye forgot the hat. She walked to the light.

A dog ran by with a stick. It tripped on a drum. Boom! The drum made a funny sound. Faye did not laugh. She did not even turn her head.

The light did not move. It just shone. Faye put out her hand. Her fingers felt only cold air. The light stayed far away. It always stayed far away.

The wind grew calm. The leaf hat was gone. Faye sat down. She held her doll close. She wished and wished for the light. But she could not reach it. Not ever.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Faye

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text: A doll named Faye got a new hat. It was red with a little bow. She put it on her head. The wind blew hard. The hat went up, up, up. It did a drum roll on the fence. Then it did a bounce on the grass. Faye laughed. That was funny. She ran to get it. But she stopped. She saw a light. It was far away. It was on the other side of the playground. It was small and green. It did not move. It did not blink. It just sat there. Faye wanted it. She wanted it so much. She forgot her hat. She forgot the wind. She walked and walked. She said, I want the light. I want the light. I want the light. She said it again and again. The wind pushed her back. She did not care. She wanted the light. She wanted to hold it. She wanted to be calm near it. But the light stayed far. It stayed small. It stayed green. Faye sat down. Her hat was gone. The light was still far. She cried.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Next to the candle, Anya put a hat on her doll. The hat was red and soft. It had a little bow. Anya clapped her hands. "You look so pretty," she said.

That night, Anya could not sleep. She looked out her window. Far away, high up on a mountain, she saw a small green light. It blinked and blinked. It looked like a tiny star that fell down low.

Anya did not know what it was. She put her hand on the glass. She could not reach it. It was too far.

The next day was sunny. Anya played with her doll all day. The doll wore the red hat. They had tea and cake. Anya laughed and laughed. She forgot the light.

But at night, she looked again. The little light was still there, far away. It made her feel quiet.

Then her mom came in. "Time to sleep, my love," she said. She kissed Anya's head. Anya held her doll close. The doll's hat was warm. Anya closed her eyes. The green light kept blinking on the mountain, but Anya felt happy. She had her doll, her hat, and her mom. She slept.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Nana the doll got a new hat. Anya made it from soft red cloth. She put it on Nana's head. The hat had a little bow.

Anya sat by the window. Her candle made a small warm glow. Far away, high up on a mountain, she saw a tiny green light. It blinked like a firefly. She wanted to reach it. But the mountain was far and the night was dark.

"One day," Anya said. She kissed Nana's hat.

The next day was sunny. Anya played outside with Nana. She looked up at the mountain. The green light was gone.

That night, she saw it again. It was so high. So far. She held her candle close.

"Maybe it is a star," she said.

"Maybe it is someone's lamp," said Mama.

Anya thought about the light a lot. But Nana's hat was here. Nana was here. Anya hugged her doll.

Then Papa came home. He had a surprise. A tiny green lamp for Anya's room. It glowed soft and kind.

"The mountain light is far," Papa said. "But this one is for you."

Anya put the lamp by her bed. She put Nana beside it. The hat looked pretty in the green glow. Anya smiled and closed her eyes. She did not need to reach anymore. Her light was home.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Nora the doll got a new hat. Anya put it on Nora. The hat was soft and blue. Anya clapped her hands.

That night, Anya lit a candle. She held Nora up to the window. Far away, high on a mountain, a small green light was shining. Anya tried to reach it with her hand. The glass was cold. The light stayed far.

The next day was sunny. Anya and Nora played outside. But Anya kept looking at the mountain. The green light was gone in the day.

At night, the light came back. Anya held Nora close. "Do you see it?" she asked. Nora did not answer. Nora just smiled with her painted mouth.

Anya hugged Nora and the soft blue hat. "We do not need to touch it," she said. "We can love it from here."

The green light blinked, like a small kind eye. Anya felt warm inside. She blew out the candle and went to sleep. Nora slept too, wearing her new hat.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Nya had a doll. The doll had a new hat. The hat was small and blue. Anya loved the hat.

She put it on the doll. She made the doll dance. Then she saw the light. It was high on the mountain. It was far away.

Anya went to the window. The light was so small. It was like a tiny star. She wanted to touch it. She put her doll down.

She went outside. The night was dark. She walked up the hill. The light was still far. She said, "I want to reach it."

She walked more. Her feet hurt. The light was always high. She did not stop. She held her doll's hat. The hat was in her hand.

Then a candle was in a window. A kind person said, "Come in." Anya sat down. The person gave her a sunny smile.

Anya looked at the hat. She put it back on her doll. The doll looked happy. Anya was happy too. The light was still high on the mountain. But now she had a warm place.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Nia made a hat for her doll. She sewed it with red thread. The doll looked pretty. Anya loved the doll. Anya put the hat on the doll. Then Anya saw a light.

The light was high up on a mountain. It was late at night. The light was small and green. It blinked and blinked. Anya wanted it.

She held her doll. She lit a candle. The candle was warm. She said, "I want to reach it."

She walked to the mountain. The wind was cold. Her doll was in her arms. The light was far away. She said, "I want to reach it."

She climbed up and up. Her feet hurt. The light was still far. She said, "I want to reach it."

She did not stop. She held her doll tight. The hat stayed on. She said, "I want to reach it."

Then the sun came up. It was sunny. The light went away. Anya looked down. Her doll was safe. Her doll had the hat. Anya smiled. She was happy.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
Rosa the doll got a new hat. Omar put it on her head. It was blue with a little star on the side. "You look pretty," Omar said. He gave her a hug.

The morning was sunny. Omar took Rosa outside. He saw a tall tree. At the very top, a small light shone. It was green and soft. It looked like a tiny leaf that could glow. Omar wanted to touch it.

"Stay here, Rosa," he said. He put her on the grass. He began to climb. The tree was high. The light was higher. He went up and up.

Then his foot slipped. He fell down, down, down. He was not hurt. But when he looked for Rosa, she was gone. The wind had rolled her away.

Omar looked and looked. He found only her new hat. The little star was dirty. The green light still shone at the top of the tree. Omar sat on the grass and held the hat. He did not climb again.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
Rosa was a doll. Omar got her a new hat. The hat was blue with a little star on it. He put it on Rosa. He gave her a hug.

It was early morning. The sun was sunny and warm. Omar took Rosa outside. He saw a light at the very top of a tall tree. It was small and green. It blinked like a tiny leaf.

Omar wanted to touch it. He held Rosa up high. But the light was too far. He put Rosa down. The light stayed up there.

Omar tried to climb the tree. He was too small. He fell down. Rosa fell too. Her new hat came off.

Omar sat on the grass. He held Rosa and her hat. The green light blinked and blinked. It was so pretty. He wanted it so much.

The morning went away. The light went away too. Omar was sad. He put the hat back on Rosa. But the star was lost. And the light was gone.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
Rosa was a doll. She got a new hat. Omar put it on her head. The hat was red and soft. Omar was happy.

In the early morning, Omar took Rosa outside. The sky was sunny. A star was still up, small and pale. Omar saw a little green light at the top of a tall tree. It blinked like a tiny leaf. He wanted it.

He held Rosa up. "Look," he said. The light did not come down.

Omar tried to climb the tree. He was too small. He tried to call it. It did not listen. He gave Rosa a hug. Her hat fell off.

Every morning he came back. The green light stayed high. It was always there, always far. He reached and reached.

One day Rosa was gone. He lost her in the grass. The hat was gone too. Omar sat under the tree. The green light blinked at the top. He could not reach it. He could not reach anything.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
Rosa the doll got a new hat. Omar put it on her head. The hat was small and blue. It had a little star on the side. Omar was happy. He gave Rosa a hug.

Then he looked out the window. The morning was sunny and soft. Far away, high in a tall tree, a small light was shining. It was green and bright. It was at the very top.

Omar wanted to touch it. He walked outside. He stood under the tree. The light was so high. He held Rosa up. Her new hat fell off. He did not see.

He tried to climb. The tree was too tall. The light stayed at the top. It was green and far.

Omar sat down. He held Rosa close. The light kept shining. He could not reach it. He never could.

The sun went up. The light stayed green. Omar began to cry. Rosa had no hat.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
Rosa the doll got a new hat. Omar put it on her head. The hat was red and small. It made Rosa look happy.

Then Omar saw a little light. It was green and soft. It sat at the very top of a tall tree.

Omar wanted that light. He wanted it for Rosa. Early morning was cold and gray. He left Rosa in the grass.

He put his foot on a low branch. He pulled himself up. The tree was very tall.

He climbed and climbed. His hands hurt. He did not stop. The light was small and green. It was far away.

He said, "I will get it. I will get it."

He said, "I will get it. I will get it."

The sun came up. It was sunny and warm. A bird sang like a star in the sky.

Omar was near the top. He reached out. His hand was open.

Then he fell.

Rosa lay in the grass. Her new hat was gone. No one gave her a hug.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Leo

axes.where: in the dark of the woods
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
One day Leo found a doll in the yard. She had no hat, so Leo made her one. He used a big leaf and a red string.

"It fits," said Leo. "You look nice."

The doll did not talk. That was okay.

Leo gave the doll a cookie. He did not eat it. He wanted to share.

That night Leo could not sleep. He took the doll outside. The woods were dark. He walked and walked.

Far away, a tiny light glowed. It was small and green. It was not the sun.

"Come back," said Leo's mom.

"I see a light," said Leo.

He walked toward it. It never got closer. His feet got cold. He held the doll tight.

Then he heard a sound. It was a bird. The bird took the leaf hat. Off it flew.

Leo ran home. The morning was sunny. The doll had no hat again.

"I will make a new one," said Leo.

He did. This time he used a sock.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Leo

axes.where: in the dark of the woods
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
One day Leo found a doll in the grass. The doll had no hat. Leo said, "I will make you a hat." He found a big leaf. He put it on her head. "Now you look nice," he said.

That night Leo could not sleep. He looked out the window. Far away, in the dark of the woods, a tiny green light was shining. It was small and soft. Leo wanted to hold it. He walked to the trees. The light stayed far away. "Come here," Leo said. The light did not come.

He went back home. He gave the doll a cookie. "We can share," he said. But he kept looking at the woods. The green light was still there. It was like a little star that fell down low. Leo wanted it so much.

In the morning it was sunny. Leo put on the doll's leaf hat. Then he saw something. A small green bug was on the leaf. It blinked. It was the light! "You were here all along," Leo said. The doll just smiled.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Leo

axes.where: in the dark of the woods
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
One day Leo found a doll in the grass. The doll had no hat. Leo made her a hat from a leaf. He gave her a cookie. "We can share," he said.

That night Leo woke up. The moon was gone. He saw a small light far away. It was in the dark of the woods. The light was little and green. It blinked like a bug.

Leo held the doll. "Do you see it?" he asked. The doll did not talk. The light stayed far away. Leo walked to the woods. The trees were tall and black. The light was still far.

"I want to touch it," Leo said. He said it again. "I want to touch it."

Then the sky turned sunny. The light was gone. Leo looked down. The doll's leaf hat was shining. It was green. The light was not in the woods. It was on the doll's head. Leo laughed. "You had it all the time," he said.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Leo

axes.where: in the dark of the woods
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
One day Leo got a new hat for his doll. It was red and soft. He put it on her head. "You look pretty," Leo said. He gave her a cookie. He did not want to share.

Then the sky got dark. Leo looked at the woods. Deep in the dark, a small light was there. It was low and green. It did not move. Leo said, "I want to touch it."

He walked to the woods. The light stayed far away. "Come here," Leo said. The light did not come. He said it again. "Come here. Come here."

The sunny day was gone. His doll fell in the mud. He did not pick her up. He said, "Come here. Come here." His hat was lost too.

Then he saw it. The light was a firefly. It sat on his doll's new hat. The hat was on a bush. He picked up the hat and the doll. The firefly flew away. "I still want it," Leo said. But he went home.

stories.topic: a doll and her new hat
stories.name: Leo

axes.where: in the dark of the woods
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
One day Leo made a hat for his doll. He used soft red cloth. He put it on her head. "You look nice," he said. He gave her a cookie.

Then Leo saw a little light. It was far away in the dark of the woods. It was small and green. It went blink, blink. Leo wanted to touch it.

"Stay here," he told his doll. He walked to the woods. The light was always far. He walked and walked. "I want it," he said. "I want it. I want it." He said it again and again.

The night was not sunny. The trees were dark. His doll waited with the cookie.

Leo found a small green bug. It sat on a leaf. It blinked. That was the light. He could not take it. It was just a bug.

He went back home. His doll still had her hat. "I will share my cookie with you," he said. Then he put the hat on his own head and laughed.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: Pitter-patter went the rain on the roof. Tom rode his rocking horse, fast, fast, fast. "Slow down," said Mom. "You will slide off." Tom did not slow down. He rocked so hard the horse tipped. Bump! Tom fell on a soft rug. "Silly horse," said Tom. "Silly me." Mom gave him a pebble to hold for luck. Tom put it in his pocket. He rocked again, slow and soft. The rain stopped. Out the window, far away, a small light shone on top of a hill. It was green and quiet. Tom looked at it for a moment. Then he rocked his horse, nice and slow, and did not fall again.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Papa gave Tom a rocking horse. It was red and had a black tail. Tom got on and rocked. He rocked fast. The horse went too fast and Tom fell off. "Ouch," said Tom.

"You went too fast," said Papa. "Try slow."

Tom got back on. He rocked slow. Then he rocked fast again. The horse went too fast. Tom did not fall. But he felt silly.

"Look at the far hill," said Papa. "The sky is dark. A storm is coming."

Tom looked out the window. On top of the far hill, a small light was on. It was green. It blinked in the wind. Tom wanted to touch it. He did not know why.

"Papa, can we go there?" asked Tom.

"No," said Papa. "Not in this rain."

Tom rocked and rocked. The horse went too fast. A pebble hit the window. Tom did not slide off. He held on. He looked at the far hill. The green light was still there.

"Slow down," said Papa. "You will fall."

Tom slowed down. The horse stopped. The rain stopped too. Tom was safe. But he still looked at the far hill.

"Maybe tomorrow," said Papa.

Tom nodded. He patted the horse. The green light blinked once more.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Pitter-patter went the rain on the roof. Tom rode his rocking horse. It went too fast. Back and forth, back and forth, so fast the room looked like a gray blur.

"Slow down, horse," said Tom. But the horse did not slow down. It rocked harder.

Tom fell off. Bonk. He sat on the floor. A little pebble from his shoe was under him. Ouch.

"Are you okay?" said Mom.

"My horse goes too fast," said Tom. "It is silly."

"Hold the handles," said Mom.

Tom climbed back on. He held the handles tight. He made the horse slide slow. Forward, back. Forward, back. Now it was just right.

But then Tom looked out the window. On top of the far hill, a small light glowed. It was soft and far away. He wanted to touch it. He could not.

"Come eat," said Mom.

Tom rode slow. The light stayed on the hill. He looked at it again. He wished he could go there. But he held the handles and rocked, and the light blinked far away.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Papa gave Tom a rocking horse. It was red and white. Tom got on. He rocked and rocked. The horse went too fast. "Slow down!" said Tom. The horse did not slow down. Tom held on tight. He felt like a pebble in a storm.

Rain hit the window. Tom looked out. On the far hill, a small light shone. It was green. Tom wanted to touch it. He rocked faster to get there. "Stop, silly horse!" he said. The horse went faster.

"Tom, hold the mane," said Mama. Tom held the mane. The horse slowed. It began to slide soft and slow. "Good boy," said Mama.

Tom looked at the hill again. The green light was still far away. He rocked slow. He rocked fast. He rocked slow. The light did not come closer. "I want it," Tom said. "I want it. I want it."

The storm went away. Tom got off the horse. The green light stayed on the hill. Tom went to bed. He could still see it, small and far, and he wanted it still.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Pebble sat by the window while Tom rocked. The horse went too fast. It went up, down, up, down.

"Slow down," said Mom.

"I can't," said Tom.

The horse went faster. The rain hit the glass. Tom fell off. He was not hurt.

"That was silly," he said.

Then he saw it. On top of the far hill, past the wet trees, a little light was burning. It was small and green. It did not move.

Tom got back on the horse. He rocked. He looked at the light. He rocked. He looked at the light.

"I want to go there," he said.

"You can't," said Mom. "The hill is far."

"I want to go there. I want to go there."

The horse went too fast again. Tom slid off. He hit a pebble on the rug. Ouch.

Mom fixed the horse. She made it slow. Tom rocked soft. He looked at the light.

"I want to go there," he said again. Soft. Soft.

The light stayed on the hill. Tom rocked. He could not go. He could only want.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a tower far away

stories.text:
Papa gave Eli a wooden rocking horse. Its name was Dash. Eli fed Dash a pretend egg. Then Eli rocked. Dash went too fast. Back and forth, back and forth. The room went blurry. Eli held on tight.

Out the window, the wind blew. It was a windy, cold autumn evening. Eli's coat was thin. He did not want to stop. Dash went faster.

Far away, on a tall tower, a small green light blinked. It looked like a tiny star. Eli wanted to touch it. He reached out one hand. The light stayed far, far away. It always stayed far.

Eli rocked and rocked. He forgot his egg. He forgot his swing outside. He forgot his supper. He only saw the green light.

Then Dash stopped. The light blinked once and went dark. Eli sat still. His hands were empty. The tower was gone in the night. He was very small, and very cold, and all alone.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a tower far away

stories.text:
Papa gave Eli a rocking horse. It was red and big. Eli loved it. He rocked and rocked. The horse went fast. Too fast. "Slow down," said Mama. Eli did not slow down.

It was a cold autumn evening. The wind was windy. Eli rocked by the window. He ate one egg for supper. Then he saw a light. It was on a tower far away. The light was small and green. It blinked once.

Eli rocked faster. The horse went fast, too fast. He wanted to reach the light. He rocked and rocked.

The light blinked again. It was far, far away. Eli could not go there. He was too small. He could only rock.

He went to the swing outside. He swung high. He looked for the light. It was gone.

The night got dark. The tower was black. Eli felt sad. He went inside. He sat on the rocking horse. It did not go fast now. He held the horse and wished for the light. But the light did not come back.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a tower far away

stories.text:
Papa gave Eli a rocking horse. It was red and white. Eli loved it. He rocked and rocked. But the horse went too fast. It rocked like a windy storm. Eli held on tight.

One cold autumn evening, Eli looked out the window. Far away, a green light glowed on a tower. It was small and bright. Eli wanted to touch it. He rocked toward the window. The horse went faster.

"Stop," Eli said. But the horse did not stop. It went faster and faster. Eli saw the light. It was so far.

He tried to eat his egg, but he could not. He tried to swing outside, but he could not. The light called him.

"Come," it said. "Come here."

Eli rocked all night. The green light stayed far away. The tower was too high. The light was too far. Eli cried.

The horse went too fast and broke. The light did not come closer. Eli sat on the floor. He was sad. The green light was still far away.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a tower far away

stories.text:
Please go slow, Eli said to the rocking horse. But the horse ran fast. Too fast. Eli held on tight. His room felt small and warm, but the horse went faster.

Outside, the evening was cold. The wind was windy. Leaves blew past the window. Eli saw a tower far away. On the tower, a small green light shone.

Eli wanted that light. He rocked harder. The horse went faster. He did not stop for his egg at supper. He did not go to the swing in the yard. He just rocked and looked at the green light.

The light was far. It was always far. It blinked and blinked, like it was calling him.

Eli reached out his hand. He could not touch it. The horse went faster and faster.

The green light stayed on the tower. It never came closer.

Eli got tired. His hands slipped. The horse kept going without him. He sat on the floor and cried. The light blinked on, far away, and he was all alone.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a tower far away

stories.text:
Papa gave Eli a rocking horse. It went too fast. Eli held on tight.

Then Eli saw a green light on a tower far away. It was a cold autumn evening. The light was small and green.

Eli wanted the light. He rocked fast. He rocked faster.

"Stop," said Mama. "You will fall."

But Eli rocked. The room was windy. His egg rolled off the table. It broke.

Eli did not stop. He rocked like a swing. Back and forth. Back and forth.

The green light blinked. Eli reached out. He could not touch it. It was too far.

He rocked harder. The horse went too fast. Eli fell down. He cried.

The light stayed on the tower. Far, far away.

Eli got up. He rocked again. He reached again. The light did not come.

Night came. The light was still there. Eli was small. The tower was tall. He could not reach the green light. He never would.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Giddy-up went the rocking horse. Sid rode it fast. Too fast! The horse went bump, bump, bump. Sid held on tight. Rain tapped the window. It was a rainy evening.

Sid played in the house. He lit a candle. The flame did a little dance. Then Sid saw something out the window. A small light blinked in the dark of the woods.

Sid was not brave about the woods. But he wanted that light. He ran outside. The rain made him shake. He slipped in a mud puddle. Splat! His boots went one way. Sid went the other way. That was funny.

The light was still far away. It was small and green. Sid reached for it. His hand came back wet and empty.

He went inside. He got back on the horse. Giddy-up went the rocking horse. It went too fast again. But Sid kept looking out the window at the dark woods.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Good rain fell on the roof. Sid rode his rocking horse. It went too fast. Back and forth, back and forth. “Slow down,” said Sid. The horse did not slow down.

Sid went outside to find his candle. The woods were dark. Rain went drip, drip on his nose. He was brave. He did not shake.

Then he saw it. A small green light, deep in the dark of the woods. It blinked like a tiny star.

“Hello?” said Sid. The light did not come closer. It only blinked.

He took one step. Then two. His feet got muddy. Splash! He fell in a puddle. Mud on his chin. Mud on his nose. That was funny. He laughed.

The green light blinked far away. He reached out his hand. He could not touch it.

He went home and rode his horse again. Back and forth. The green light blinked in his window. He reached. It stayed far.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Giddy-up, said Sid. He rode his rocking horse. It went too fast. Back and forth, back and forth. The horse made a creak-creak sound.

Rain tapped the window. It was a rainy evening. Sid held a candle. The flame went wiggle-wiggle. He did not shake. He felt brave.

Then he saw a small light. It was green. It was far away in the dark of the woods. It blinked like a tiny eye.

Sid wanted that light. He got off the horse. He walked to the door.

The horse rocked by itself. It went too fast. It bumped the table. A spoon flew up and landed on Sid's head. Plop! Sid laughed. That was funny.

He looked at the woods again. The green light was still there. He reached out his hand. He could not touch it.

He climbed back on the horse. He rocked slow. He rocked fast. The green light stayed far away.

Giddy-up, he said again. But he kept looking at the light.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Giddy-up, Sid said to his rocking horse. It went too fast. It went so fast it rocked right out the door.

Rain fell on Sid's nose. The woods were dark. He held his candle. It made a small, warm dot.

Then he saw it. A green light, deep in the trees. It blinked like a sleepy bug.

Sid forgot his horse. He walked toward the light. The rain went drip, drip on his hood.

His horse came too. It rocked fast on the wet leaves. It bumped a tree. Plop! Sid fell in a puddle. That was funny. He laughed.

He got up. He was brave. His knees did a little shake. The light was still there. He wanted it. He reached out.

His hand closed on air. The light stayed far away. Always far away.

Sid stood in the rain. He watched the green light. He could not have it. He could not reach it. Not tonight.

The candle went out. The light stayed on.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Good rain tapped the roof. Sid rode his rocking horse. It went too fast. It went so fast the room went blurry.

Then he saw it. A small green light, deep in the dark of the woods. It blinked and blinked.

Sid got off the horse. He took a candle. He was not brave. But he went out.

The rain was cold. The woods were dark. The green light stayed far away.

He ran. He tripped on a root. His candle fell in a puddle. Pfft. He looked like a wet frog. That was funny.

He got up. He reached. The light moved back.

Want it. Reach it. Can't have it. Want it. Reach it. Can't have it.

His hands began to shake. The light blinked on.

Want it. Reach it. Can't have it. Want it. Reach it. Can't have it.

He walked home slow. The rocking horse still went too fast. The green light blinked in the dark of the woods. Sid watched from his window. He reached. He could not touch it.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Sally the rocking horse went too fast. Ella held on tight. Back and forth, back and forth, so fast the room blurred. Her hands grew hot. Her tummy felt lumpy and strange.

"Slow down," said her friend Ben. He put a cookie on the floor. Sally stopped. Ella ate the cookie. She felt better.

They went outside. The sun was warm. Ella saw something far away. High up on a mountain, a small light shone. It was pale and quiet. It looked like a tiny star that forgot to go home. Ella tried to draw it with her finger. She could not reach it. She waved anyway. The light did not wave back.

Ben said, "Let's play tag." So they ran. Ella forgot the light for a while. But once, she looked up. It was still there. Just a little bit. She smiled and ran on.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Soon Ella rode the rocking horse. It went too fast. Back and forth, back and forth, so fast her hair flew. Her friend Sam sat on the floor. He held a cookie and said, "Slow down, Ella."

But Ella did not slow down. The horse went faster.

Out the window, the sun was warm. The afternoon was bright. High up on a mountain, far away, a small light shone. It was tiny and green. Ella wanted to touch it. She leaned forward. The horse tipped.

Sam caught her. "Whoa," he said. He gave her the cookie. It was lumpy and warm.

Ella looked at the mountain again. The light was still there. She tried to draw it on paper. Her lines came out wobbly. "I want to go there," she said.

"You can't," said Sam. "But I will sit with you."

They rocked slowly. The light blinked on the mountain. Ella felt it pull her, soft and far. Sam held her hand. The afternoon turned gold. The little light stayed where it was. Ella stopped reaching. She just looked.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Sometimes Ella rides the rocking horse too fast. It creaks and tips, and her hair flies back. "Slow down," says her friend Sam. He holds a cookie in one hand. "You will fall."

Ella slows the horse. Then she sees it. Far away, high up on a mountain, a small green light shines in the sunny afternoon. It is tiny, like a far-off star that stayed for lunch. Her chest goes tight. She wants to go there.

"Come on," she says. Sam gives her the cookie. They walk past the lumpy hill and the old fence. The light stays high. It never gets closer.

"We can draw it," Sam says. So they sit. Ella draws the mountain. She draws the light on top. Her horse would never climb that far. Her legs are too short.

She looks up again. The light is still there, small and bright. It does not need her. But she needs it.

"Maybe tomorrow," Sam says.

Ella nods. They walk home. The light stays up on the mountain, blinking like it knows her name.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Sometimes Ella rode the rocking horse too fast. It went back and forth, back and forth, until the room turned to sky. Her friend Sam held her elbow. "Slow down," he said. Ella did not slow down.

On a sunny afternoon she saw it. High up on a mountain sat a small green light. It blinked like a faraway star. It was so high. It was so bright. Ella wanted to touch it.

She tried to draw the light with a cookie in her hand. The line came out lumpy. Sam said, "That is a nice try." But Ella only looked up.

The horse kept rocking. It went faster. The green light stayed far away. Sam put his hand on the horse's head. "Stop now," he said. "Please."

Ella slowed. The light still blinked. It was still far. She ate her cookie and gave Sam half. The green light watched from the mountain. It did not come down. Ella did not go up. But she thought of it. She thought of it all day.

stories.topic: a rocking horse that goes too fast
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: high up on a mountain

stories.text:
Sometimes Ella rides the rocking horse. It goes too fast. Back and forth, back and forth, so fast the room spins.

Then she sees it. A small light. High on a mountain. It shines in the sunny afternoon.

"Look," she says. Her friend Ben looks. "I don't see it," he says. He gives her a cookie. It is lumpy and warm. She eats it fast.

The horse rocks. The light stays up there. She wants to draw it, but she can't. Her hand shakes. The horse is too fast.

"Slow down," Ben says.

She can't slow down. The light is up there. It is far. It is small. It never comes closer.

Up. Down. Up. Down. The sunny afternoon goes on. Ben holds her hand.

"Please," she says. Not to Ben. To the light. The light says nothing. It just shines.

The horse goes faster. Her eyes stay up. She never gets there. The light is up there. She is down here. Always.

stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
Night came early and made the sky purple. Eli sat on the porch steps. The summer sunset was hiding behind big gray clouds.

"Will the fireflies come out?" Eli asked.

"Not in this rain," said Mom.

Eli counted fat drops on the rail. Then he saw a far little light down the street. It sat on a car parked by the corner. It did not move. It did not blink. It just held still, like a warm stone in all that wet.

Eli ran to the fence and held the cold bars. The light stayed small and far. He could not reach it.

The storm blew harder. A bug buzzed and tried to spin in the wind.

"Come inside," said Mom. "I made cocoa. It's cozy."

Eli went in. He drank his cocoa and watched the window. Soon the clouds broke. The sky turned orange and pink. Fireflies rose from the grass, one by one. They made their own small lights, right here, close enough to touch. Eli smiled. The far light could wait.

stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
Night came early with rain, and Eli sat on the porch watching the summer sun melt low behind the clouds. He had a jar for fireflies, but the storm kept them hidden. A wet stone sat in his pocket, smooth and warm from his hand.

Down the street, a car was parked under the dark trees. Its little light blinked on and off. Eli could not stop looking at it. It was small and far, like a star that fell too close to the road.

"Stay cozy inside," said his mom.

"I'm just looking," Eli said.

The rain tapped the roof. He spun the jar lid in his fingers. The light blinked. He thought of fireflies, how they glow and go, glow and go.

"Will they come out?" he asked.

"After the storm," she said.

He waited. The light down the street blinked again, soft and steady, and Eli felt a tug in his chest, like he wanted to walk to it but his feet stayed put.

stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
Night came slow on Eli’s street. The summer sunset turned the sky pink and gold. Fireflies blinked in the yard like tiny stars. Eli sat on a warm stone and watched them.

“Do you see that?” said Mom. “The storm is coming.”

Wind pushed the trees. Rain tapped the roof. Eli ran to the window. The fireflies hid. The sunset went gray.

Then he saw it. Far down the street, on an old car, a little light glowed. It was green and soft. It did not blink like fireflies. It just stayed.

“Can we go see?” Eli asked.

“Not in this rain,” said Mom.

Eli tried to spin his top. He tried to get cozy under a blanket. But his eyes kept going back to the car.

The storm left. The fireflies came out again. The sunset came back, orange and low. Eli looked down the street. The green light was still there.

“Maybe tomorrow,” he whispered.

He watched it until bedtime. He did not reach it. But he liked knowing it was there.

stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
Night came early with rain. Eli sat on the porch. He watched the sky turn from gray to gold. Summer sunsets were his favorite. But the fireflies were late. The storm made them hide.

"Eli, come in," said Mom. "It's wet."

"I'm waiting," Eli said. "They always come."

He held a warm stone in his hand. He liked to spin it. It felt cozy and safe.

Then he saw it. Far down the street, on a car, a small light. Not a firefly. A little shine. It blinked once. It blinked twice. Eli stood up.

"Where are you going?" Mom asked.

"Just looking," Eli said.

The rain stopped. The sun went down. Fireflies lifted from the grass. They made small green dots. But Eli watched the car. The light stayed on. It was far away. He could not reach it. He took one step. Then another. The fireflies followed him. But his eyes stayed on that shine. It was always there. Always far.

stories.name: Eli

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
Nights came slow in summer. Eli sat on the porch. The sky turned pink and gold. Fireflies blinked in the yard. It was cozy and warm.

“Look, Eli. The little lights,” said Mom.

“I see them,” Eli said.

Then he saw a different light. Far down the street, a car was parked. A small light shone on it. It was not yellow like the fireflies. It was green.

Eli stood up. He walked down the steps. He did not feel the stone path under his feet.

“Where are you going?” Mom called.

He did not answer. The light was small. It was far. He wanted to touch it.

The wind blew. Rain started. Eli kept walking. The fireflies hid. The sky went gray.

“Come back!” Mom called.

He turned. The light was still there. He took a step toward it. Then another. The rain did not stop him. Nothing stopped him.

“Eli!”

He did not hear her. He only saw the green light. It was far away. It was always far away. He reached. He reached. He reached.

stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Mama called Kai in from the yard. The sun was going down, slow and orange. Kai did not want to go inside. It was almost bedtime.

"Just five more minutes," Kai said.

"Five more," Mama said. "Then bed."

Kai sat on the grass and ate a cold apple. The sky turned pink, then red. Fireflies came out, one by one. They blinked like tiny lamps over the lawn.

"Look," Kai said. "They float."

Mama sat down too. They were quiet together.

Out on the lake, a small boat rocked. A little light shone on it, far away. Kai watched it for a moment. Then he forgot it.

A firefly landed on Kai's hand. It blinked once, twice, and flew off.

"Time for bed," Mama said.

"Okay," Kai said. He did not fuss.

He learned something soft that night. You can let a small light go, and still keep the warm.

stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Mama called Kai inside just before bedtime. The sky turned soft and pink. It was summer, and the fireflies came out to play.

"Look, Mama," said Kai. "One firefly sits on my apple."

"Say goodnight," Mama said. "It is late."

Kai ran to the window. Out on the lake, a boat sat still. A small light shone on the boat. It was pale and far away. It did not blink like the fireflies. It just glowed.

"Can we go see it?" Kai asked.

"No, sweet, the boat is too far," Mama said.

Kai watched the little light float on the quiet water. It felt like a wish he could not hold.

"Goodnight, little light," he whispered.

The fireflies near his window blinked and blinked. They were close. They were his.

The far light stayed far. The near lights stayed near. Some lights we reach, and some we only love from here.

stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text: Maybe the best part of summer is when the sky turns pink and orange. Kai sat on the porch with his dad. It was almost bedtime. The sun went down slow over the lake. "Look," said Dad. "Here come the fireflies." Little bugs blinked in the yard. Kai ran to catch one. He did not catch it. He ate a small apple and watched. Then he saw a light far out on the lake. It was small and green. It sat on a boat. The boat did not move. It just did. The light made a soft glow on the water. "Can we go see it?" Kai asked. "Not tonight," said Dad. "It is bedtime." Kai stood quiet. The green light seemed to float. He wanted to touch it. He wanted it more than the fireflies. Every night he looked for it. Every night it stayed far away. "Why can I not reach it?" he asked. "Some lights are for looking," said Dad. Kai learned that night that not all pretty things are for keeping. Some are just for loving from far away.

stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Mama called Kai inside just before bedtime. The sun was going down, all orange and pink over the lake. Fireflies blinked in the yard like tiny stars.

"Time to wash up," Mama said.

"Five more minutes," Kai said.

He ate his apple on the porch steps. The fireflies danced. He tried to catch one, but they always slipped away. Then he saw it. Out on the lake, a little boat rocked on the water. On the boat, a small green light. It glowed and blinked, soft and low.

"Can I go see it?" Kai asked.

"See what?" said Mama.

"The light. On the boat."

"No boat tonight. It is bedtime."

The fireflies floated near his hands. But Kai just watched the boat. The green light blinked. Blinked. He wanted to touch it. He wanted it so much.

"Come inside," Mama said.

"I want the light," Kai said. "I want the light."

"You cannot have everything you want," Mama said, soft and quiet a moment. "But you can love what is here."

Kai looked at the fireflies. One landed on his finger. It was small, and green, and close. He smiled. The far light blinked on. But now he had one of his own.

stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Mama called Kai to come inside. The sun was going down. The sky was pink and orange.

"Look at the fireflies," Mama said. "They blink in the grass."

Kai nodded. But his eyes went to the lake. On the water, a small boat floated alone. A tiny green light shone on its side. It was far away. It was so small.

"Time for bed," Papa said. "Bring your apple."

Kai held his apple. He did not eat it. He looked at the little green light.

"Can I touch the boat?" Kai asked.

"No, sweetie," Mama said. "It is too far."

"It is just a lamp," Papa said.

Kai shook his head. "I want to go there."

"Say goodnight to the fireflies," Mama said.

Kai whispered, "Goodnight."

But the green light stayed in his eyes. Float, float, float. Quiet, quiet, quiet. He wanted it. He wanted the little green light. He wanted the boat. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it.

"Kai, close your eyes," Mama said.

"I want the light," Kai said. "I want the light."

"The light is far," Papa said. "Some things we can see but not hold."

Kai shut his eyes. The green glow stayed.

Moral: Some pretty things are ours only to watch.

stories.name: Gus

axes.where: on a train going by

stories.text:
Right before the sun went down, Gus ran to the field with his pail. He wanted to catch fireflies. The summer sky turned pink and orange. It was warm and sticky. Gus tried to swim in the tall grass. That made him laugh. He fell down. His pail rolled away.

Then a train went by. It was loud and fast. Gus sat up. He saw a small green light on the last car. It was bright and far away. He wanted to touch it. He reached out his hand. The train took the light down the track. It was gone.

Gus looked for fireflies again. He waited and waited. But the sky got dark. No little lights came. He held his empty pail. He walked home alone.

stories.name: Gus

axes.where: on a train going by

stories.text:
Right after breakfast, Gus ran to the porch to watch the summer sunset. But the sky was still soft and gray. The sun was not ready. The fireflies were not ready.

Gus did not mind. He had a pail. He had big plans to swim. He sat on the steps with sticky jam on his hands.

Then a train went by. Click, clack, click. One small light glowed on the last car. It was green. Gus stood up. He reached out. The train took the light away.

He laughed. "My hands are sticky!" he said. He waved at nobody. Then he sat down again.

All day he waited for the sunset. He waited for the fireflies. The sun went down. The sky turned pink and gold.

The fireflies came. They blinked and blinked. Gus ran to catch them. But they were not green like that light.

The train did not come back. Gus held his empty pail. He did not swim. He sat very still, and the fireflies lit the dark.

stories.name: Gus

axes.where: on a train going by

stories.text: Right before bed, Gus ran outside with his pail. He wanted to swim in the warm evening air. The sunset made the sky pink and orange. Fireflies blinked like tiny stars. Gus tried to catch them. His hands got sticky from the grass. He laughed when a firefly landed on his nose. Then he heard a train. It went by slow. On the train, one small light glowed green. It was not a firefly. It was not the sun. Gus reached for it. The train moved on. The green light went far away. He wanted it so much. He reached again. The train was gone. The fireflies came back, but Gus did not see them. He only saw the green light in his mind. His pail sat empty. He did not swim. He went to bed sad. The green light stayed far away, always going.

stories.name: Gus

axes.where: on a train going by

stories.text:
Right before the sun went down, Gus ran to the field with his pail. He loved summer sunsets. The sky turned pink and orange. Fireflies blinked like tiny stars. He tried to catch them in his pail, but they flew too high. He laughed when one landed on his nose. It ticked.

Then he heard a train. It rolled slow and long. A small light shone on the last car. It was green. Gus forgot the fireflies. He wanted that light. He wanted to swim in it. He reached out, but the train was too far. His hands felt sticky from the grass.

Every morning he came back. The sun was barely up. He waited for the train. He saw the green light again. It was so close. It was so far. He ran beside the tracks. He tripped and fell. The light moved away.

The fireflies were gone. The summer was gone. Gus sat alone. He never caught the light. He never caught anything at all.

stories.name: Gus

axes.where: on a train going by

stories.text: Right before the sun went down, Gus ran to the field with his pail. He loved summer sunsets and fireflies. The sky turned pink and orange. Fireflies blinked like tiny stars. Gus tried to catch them. He got sticky from the grass. He laughed when a firefly sat on his nose. He wanted to swim in the light. Then he heard a train. It went by slow. A small green light shone on the last car. It was far away. Gus reached for it. The train took the light away. He ran after it. His pail fell. The light got smaller. It was gone. He sat in the dark. The fireflies came back. But Gus did not look at them. He only looked down the track. He whispered, I want the light. I want the light. I want the light.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
I like summer sunsets best. Cleo sat on the porch and watched the sky turn pink and orange. Soon the fireflies would come out. They blinked like tiny stars.

"Will they come tonight?" asked her little brother, Sam.

"They always come," said Cleo. "Just wait."

The air felt warm. Mom brought out cookies she had tried to bake. They were a little burnt, but Cleo ate two anyway.

Then the wind picked up. Clouds rolled in. Rain fell fast and hard.

"No fireflies," said Sam, sad.

Cleo looked toward the sea. Far away, a lighthouse blinked on. It was not white. It was a soft green light. It turned and turned in the storm.

Cleo wished she could touch it. She reached out her hand. But the light stayed far away, over the cold water.

"Come inside," said Mom.

Cleo didn't move. She just watched the green light, slow and steady, while the rain hit the roof.

Then the clouds broke. The sun came back low and red. And one by one, the fireflies rose from the wet grass.

"See?" said Cleo. "I told you."

The green light kept turning. Cleo turned away from it, and watched the fireflies instead.

stories.name: Cleo

features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
In the summer, Cleo loved to watch the sky turn orange and pink. She sat on the porch with her grandpa. The air was warm. It smelled like rain. A storm was coming.

"Look," Grandpa said. "The fireflies are early."

The little bugs blinked in the yard. They looked like tiny stars. Cleo ran to catch one. She did not catch any.

Then she saw a different light. It was far away, on a lighthouse by the sea. It went round and round. Cleo stopped. She wanted to touch it.

"Can we go there?" she asked.

"Not today," Grandpa said. "The storm is too big."

Cleo watched the light. It felt like a friend. She reached for it. It was too far.

The rain came. It fell hard. Cleo went inside. They had to bake a cake for the storm. The moon hid behind clouds.

Later, the rain stopped. The fireflies came back. One landed on Cleo's hand. She smiled. The lighthouse light was still there. But now she did not need to reach for it. She had a light of her own.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
I was watching the summer sunset with Cleo. The sky turned pink and orange. Soon the fireflies would come out. They blink like tiny lamps in the grass.

Cleo pointed at the sea. "Look there," she said.

A lighthouse stood on the rocks. Its light was green. It spun around and around. Cleo watched it. She forgot the sunset. She forgot the fireflies.

"I want to touch it," she said.

"You can't," I said. "It is far away."

The wind grew strong. Clouds hid the sun. A storm came fast. We ran to the porch.

Cleo kept looking at the sea. "The light is still there," she said. "It is always there."

The rain fell hard. The moon hid. We could not bake our cookies. We stayed warm inside.

Then the storm stopped. The sky cleared. Fireflies came out again.

"Look," I said. "They are like small green lights."

Cleo smiled. "They are close," she said. "I can catch one."

She did. The little light blinked in her hands. The lighthouse light still spun, but Cleo watched the firefly now.

stories.name: Cleo

stories.text: In the summer, Cleo loved to watch the sunset. She would sit on the porch and wait for the sky to turn pink. Then the fireflies came out. They blinked like tiny stars. Cleo tried to catch them in her jar. "Come here, little bugs," she said. But they always flew away. The air was warm and smelled like grass. Mama said, "Time to bake the pie." Cleo went inside. But through the window, she saw something else. Far away, on a lighthouse by the sea, a small green light glowed. It was not a firefly. It was steady and bright. Cleo wanted to touch it. She reached out her hand. The storm clouds rolled in. The green light stayed on. "I want that light," Cleo whispered. She forgot the pie. She forgot the fireflies. "I want it. I want it. I want it." Mama said, "Cleo, the moon is up." But Cleo only saw the green light. Then the light went out. The storm had knocked the power down. Cleo blinked. The fireflies were back. She smiled and caught one at last.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
I love summer sunsets with Cleo. We sit on the porch and watch the sky turn pink. Then the fireflies come out. Little dots of light. Blink, blink, blink.

"Look, Cleo!" I say. But Cleo does not look at the fireflies. She looks past them. She looks at the sea.

On the rocks by the water stands a lighthouse. A small green light burns on top. It is a stormy afternoon. The wind pulls my hair. The waves hit hard. But that green light stays on.

Cleo stands up. She walks to the fence. "I want to touch it," she says.

"You can't," I say. "It is far away."

"I want to hold it," she says. "I want to keep it."

The fireflies blink near her hands. She does not see them. She only sees the green light. She reaches out. Her fingers close on air.

"I want it," she says. "I want it. I want it."

The sun goes down. The moon comes up. Mom calls us in to bake bread. The warm kitchen smells good. Cleo sits by the window. She watches the lighthouse still.

Then she laughs. "Fireflies are little lights too," she says. "I can catch those." And she runs outside to try.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
Fireflies came out when the summer sunset turned the sky pink. Tom sat on the porch with his friend Ben. They ate warm cake from a plate. It was a sunny day that ended in rain. Little drops fell on the roof.

"Look," Ben said. He pointed at the field.

Bugs blinked like tiny lamps. Tom laughed when one landed on his nose. Ben tried to push it away. He slipped in the mud instead. They both giggled.

Far off, past the wet trees, a lighthouse stood by the sea. Its light went round and round. Tom saw it once and thought, that is a nice light. It never comes closer. But he had cake and a friend. That was enough tonight.

The rain stopped. The fireflies stayed. Tom and Ben watched until the sky went dark. Then they went inside.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
Fireflies came out when the summer sun went down. Tom loved to watch them blink over the grass. One night, his friend Mia brought cake. They sat on the porch and ate it with their hands. The cake was messy and sweet. Tom laughed when Mia got frosting on her nose.

Then rain began to fall. The fireflies hid. Tom felt sad. Mia gave him a gentle push. "Let's go inside," she said.

But Tom looked past the trees, toward the sea. Far away, a lighthouse stood on a rock. Its light turned round and round, slow and steady. It was not a firefly. It was not the sun. But it called to him. He wanted to touch it. He wanted to stand under it. He could not. The sea was too wide.

"Come on," Mia said. "You're getting wet."

Tom smiled. He ate one more piece of cake. The rain tapped the roof. He thought of the lighthouse light. It was still turning. It would turn all night. Maybe tomorrow would be sunny. Maybe he would see it again.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
Fireflies came out when the summer sunset turned the sky pink. Tom ran through the grass. He caught bugs in a jar. His friend Meg ran too. They had cake on a blanket. It was sunny all day. Now the sky was soft.

Then Tom saw it. Far away, a light blinked on a lighthouse by the sea. The rain made the window wet. The light was small and green. Tom wanted to touch it. He could not.

"Push me higher," Tom said. He climbed a tree. The light stayed far. Meg laughed when he slipped. "You look like a wet frog," she said. Tom laughed too.

The rain got harder. The fireflies hid. The green light kept blinking. Tom watched it. He forgot the cake. He forgot the jar. Meg pulled his hand. "Come inside," she said.

But Tom looked back. The light blinked. It blinked and blinked. He wanted it. He wanted it so much. He could not say why. "Come on," Meg said. Tom turned away. The light blinked behind the rain.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
Fireflies came out slow on the warm night. Tom sat on the porch with his friend Ben. They had cake on paper plates. Summer was almost done.

Then Tom saw it. Far off, past the wet trees, a small light blinked on the lighthouse by the sea.

“Look,” Tom said. “It wants me to come.”

“It’s a rainy evening,” Ben said. “That light is just a light.”

Tom stood up. He tried to push through the muddy yard. His boots stuck. He fell on his back in the grass. Ben laughed so hard he dropped his cake.

“You look like a turtle,” Ben said.

Tom laughed too, but only for a second. His eyes went back to the lighthouse. Blink. Blink.

“I want to touch it,” Tom said. “I want to hold it.”

“You can’t,” Ben said. “It’s far.”

“I want it,” Tom said. “I want it. I want it.”

Ben took his hand. “Stay here. The fireflies are close.”

But Tom kept watching the small light. Blink. Blink. It was not sunny there, he knew. Still he wanted it. He always would.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
Fireflies came out when the summer sun went down. Tom loved to watch them blink. He and his friend Ben sat on the porch with cake. It was a sunny day that turned soft and gold.

Then the rain came. It tapped the roof. Tom ran to the window. Far away, by the sea, a lighthouse light went round and round. It was small and far. Tom wanted it. He wanted to hold it.

"Tom," said Ben. "You are staring again."

"I want that light," Tom said. "I want that light. I want that light."

The rain got harder. The fireflies hid. But the lighthouse light kept turning. Tom did not eat his cake. He did not laugh.

Ben gave him a push. "Let's race to the kitchen!" Tom tripped on a rug and fell into a basket. They both laughed. It was funny.

But then Tom looked out again. The light was still there. Still far. Still not his. He whispered, "I want that light."

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Noah

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text: A pony named Pip lost a shoe. Noah looked for it in the dusty yard. His friend Mia came to help. They looked under the wagon and by the old jar. No shoe. Pip stamped his foot. Then Noah saw something. On the other side of the fence, a small green light sat on a post. It was tiny and bright in the sunny afternoon. Noah wanted to touch it. He tried to climb the fence. He could not reach. Mia said, “Look here!” She found the shoe in the grass. Noah laughed. He put the shoe on Pip. The green light stayed on the post. Noah waved good-bye to it. Then he and Mia rode Pip home.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Noah

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text:
A pony can lose a shoe in the soft dusty grass. Noah saw it happen. The pony took one hop and the shoe came off. It rolled near the fence.

Noah wanted to help. He asked his friend Mia to come. They looked in the tall grass. Noah found an old jar. He put the shoe inside so it would not get lost.

Then Noah saw a small green light. It sat on the other side of the fence. The light was far away. It made him feel quiet.

"Come on," said Mia. "We can climb the fence later."

They gave the shoe back to the pony. The pony was happy. Noah was happy too.

That afternoon, the sun was warm. Noah looked at the fence once more. The green light was still there. It was small and far. He reached for it. He could not touch it.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Noah

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text:
A pony can lose a shoe on a dusty path. Noah saw it happen. The little pony went clippity-clop and then clippity. One shoe was gone.

Noah looked on the ground. He saw a jar, some rocks, and old grass. No shoe. His friend Mia came to help.

They walked by the fence. On the other side, a small green light sat in the sunny afternoon. It glowed on the grass. Noah wanted it. He did not know why.

"Come on," Mia said. "We need the shoe."

Noah put his hand on the fence. He did not climb. He looked at the light. It was so close.

They found the shoe in the dusty dirt by a tree. The pony was happy.

Noah looked back. The green light was still there, on the other side of the fence. He reached for it. His hand touched wood.

Mia took his hand. "Time to go."

Noah nodded. But he looked back one more time. The green light stayed. He could not have it.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Noah

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text:
A pony can lose a shoe in the tall grass. Noah looked for it near the dusty barn. His pony, Pip, stood still and sad. Noah wanted to help his friend.

Then Noah saw it. A small green light sat on the other side of a fence. It blinked in the sunny afternoon. Noah forgot the shoe. He walked to the fence.

“Come back,” said Mia, his friend. “We need the shoe.”

Noah did not turn. The light pulled him. He tried to climb the fence. He put one foot on a rail. The light stayed far away. He could not reach it.

Mia brought a jar. “Put the light inside,” she said. “Then you can hold it.”

Noah held the jar up. The light did not go in. It only blinked and blinked. Noah reached and reached.

“The shoe,” Mia said. “Pip needs you.”

Noah looked back. Pip waited by the dusty barn. Noah found the shoe in the grass. But all afternoon, he kept looking at the fence. The green light blinked. He still wanted it. He could not have it.

stories.text:
A pony can lose a shoe. Noah saw that the pony lost a shoe. The pony was dusty and sad. Noah said, "I will find it." His friend Mia helped him look.

On the other side of the fence, the light was there. A small green light. It sat on the grass. It glowed. Noah stopped. He forgot the shoe.

He put his hands on the fence. He did not climb. He just looked. The green light was far. It was near. It was always there.

"Noah," said Mia. "The shoe."

He looked back at the light. He reached. His fingers touched wood. The light stayed far. He reached again. The light stayed far. He reached and reached and reached.

Mia found the shoe by a jar. She said, "Noah, look."

Noah did not look. He looked at the light. The light did not come. He wanted it. He could not have it. He reached. He reached. He reached.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Gus

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Down by the barn, Gus the pony lost a shoe. It went plip into the tall grass. Gus looked and looked. The sky turned dark. Late at night, he was still looking.

His friend Bea the goat came out. "What is wrong, Gus?"

"I lost my shoe," said Gus. "I am too busy looking to sleep."

Bea helped him search. They looked under the blanket of leaves. They looked by the fence. No shoe.

Then Gus saw a small light. It was at the top of the stairs. It was green and soft. It did not bounce or blink. It just stayed there, far away.

"Bea, do you see that light?" asked Gus.

"I see it," said Bea. "But we need your shoe."

They looked again. Bea found the shoe in the mud. Gus was glad.

The green light stayed at the top of the stairs. Gus looked at it once more. Then he went to sleep.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Gus

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Down by the barn, Gus the pony hopped on three legs. His left shoe was gone. He had looked in the hay. He had looked by the fence. No shoe.

“I will help,” said Bea the hen. “We will find it.”

They looked under the red wagon. They looked in the tall grass. Bea was busy scratching. Gus was busy wishing.

Late at night, Gus could not sleep. He pulled his blanket up. Then he saw it. At the top of the stairs, a small light glowed. It was soft and green. It did not bounce. It just sat there, far away.

“Do you see that?” Gus asked.

“See what?” said Bea.

Gus took one step. The light stayed. He took two steps. The light stayed. He could not reach it.

“Come back to bed,” said Bea.

Gus went back. He lay down. The green light shone on the wall. He closed his eyes. In the morning, Bea found the shoe in the mud. But Gus still thought of the light.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Gus

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Down the lane, Gus the pony lost a shoe. He looked in the grass. He looked by the fence. No shoe.

"Help me, Bea," said Gus.

Bea the duck said, "I will help you."

They looked under the big blanket. No shoe. They looked where the rabbits bounce. No shoe.

"We must keep looking," said Bea. "Do not be busy with worry."

Late at night, Gus saw a small light. It was pale and green. It sat at the top of the stairs near the barn. It was far away. It was always far away.

"Come," said Bea. "Look here."

Gus looked at the light. He wanted to climb the stairs. He wanted to touch it. But his feet stayed down.

"Gus," said Bea. "You are kind. You are good. The shoe will come."

The light blinked. Gus took one step. Then two. But the stairs were long. The light stayed at the top.

"I want it," Gus said.

"I know," said Bea. "But I want you here."

Gus turned. In the hay, he found his shoe. The light was still there. It always was.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Gus

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Down the lane lived a pony named Gus. One of his shoes was lost in the tall grass. He looked and looked. His friend Meg came to help.

"Did you check by the fence?" Meg asked.

"Yes," said Gus. "It is not there."

They were busy all day. Gus got tired. Meg gave him a soft blanket.

Late at night, Gus went inside. He climbed the stairs to bed. At the top of the stairs, he saw a small green gleam. It was far away, past the window, past the trees. It did not bounce. It just stayed.

"I want to go there," Gus said.

"But your shoe," said Meg.

Gus took one step up. Then two. The little gleam pulled him. He forgot the grass. He forgot the fence.

"Gus, come back," said Meg.

He did not come back. He kept climbing. The gleam was so small. So far. He reached and reached. He never got there. But he kept going up.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Gus

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Down at the barn, Gus the pony lost a shoe. It fell off in the mud. Gus was sad.

His friend Mia came. "We will find it," she said.

They looked and looked. The moon was up. It was late at night.

Gus saw a little light. It was green and soft. It sat at the top of the stairs.

"Look," said Gus.

"I see only stairs," said Mia.

Gus walked to the stairs. The light did not bounce. It did not move. It just shone.

"Come back," said Mia. "You are busy with the shoe."

Gus did not hear. He put one hoof on the first step.

The light was small. It was far. It was always far.

Mia put a blanket on his back. "Please stay," she said.

Gus looked up. The light looked back.

Far. Far. Far.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
Down the path Suki rode her pony, Pip. The wind blew her hat. It was a windy morning. Clip, clop, clip, clop.

"Oh no," said Suki. Pip lost a shoe. One shoe was gone. She looked by the big tree. She looked in the tall grass. No shoe.

Suki put a jar of oats in her bag. Maybe Pip would stand still. She did not want to chase him. She wanted to find the shoe.

She walked to the far side of the playground. She saw a small shine near the swing. It was not a shoe. It was only a bit of glass.

Suki felt sad. Then she heard a clink. Her boot hit something. It was Pip's shoe! It was safe and clean in the dirt.

Suki hugged Pip. The blacksmith fixed the shoe. Pip walked home happy. Clip, clop, clip, clop. Suki was happy too.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
Down by the fence, Suki patted her pony, Pip. The wind blew hard that morning. It made the trees dance.

"Where is your shoe, Pip?" Suki asked. One shoe was gone.

Suki looked in the tall grass. She looked by the water jar. No shoe.

She ran to the playground. The wind pushed her hair. She had to chase her hat.

Then Suki saw a light. It was far away, on the far side of the playground. A small green light. It shone and shone. She wanted to touch it. But it was too far.

Suki shook her head. "Find the shoe," she said.

She looked under the slide. There it was! The lost shoe, safe and clean.

Pip was happy. Suki was happy. She put the shoe back on.

The wind blew. The green light blinked far away. Suki waved good-bye to it. Then she led Pip home.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
Down the hill ran Suki to see the pony. The windy morning blew her hair all around. The pony’s name was Pip. Pip had lost a shoe. One shoe was gone.

Suki looked by the fence. She looked in the tall grass. No shoe. She put a jar of water by Pip. Pip drank it up.

Then Suki saw a green light. It was far away, on the far side of the playground. It was small and bright. It blinked in the wind. Suki wanted to chase it. She wanted to hold it in her jar. But she had to find the shoe.

She ran back to Pip. She felt the light behind her. She turned and looked. It was still there. She wanted it. She could not have it.

Then Pip lifted a foot. The lost shoe was stuck in the mud! Suki pulled it out. She got a brush and made it clean. Pip was happy. Suki was happy too. The green light stayed far away. That was okay.

stories.topic: a pony and a lost shoe
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on the far side of the playground

stories.text:
Down at the field, Suki rode her pony, Pip. The windy morning blew her hair. Pip lost a shoe in the tall grass. They had to find it.

Suki looked and looked. The wind blew hard. She held her hat. Then she saw it. A small green light, far away, on the far side of the playground.

She wanted that light. She forgot the shoe. She ran to chase the light. "I want it," she said. "I want it. I want it."
