Ruby sat on her web. She was full. She was sad. The green light blinked once, then went dark.

stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Fuzzy Ruby the spider sat in her web. A raindrop hung on a thread. It was small and clear. Ruby wanted a drink.

The raindrop slipped. It fell on the ground. Ruby was sad. Her web was dry.

She did not brush her legs. She did not dig for bugs. She wanted that drop.

Then the sky gave more rain. Drop by drop. Ruby felt warm and happy. She drank.

But the wind came. It blew her web. The raindrop flew away.

Ruby looked across the snowy yard. Far away, a small light shone. It was little and it was green. It was on a porch. It did not move.

Ruby wanted to go there. Her legs were slow. The snow was cold. She did not reach it.

The light blinked once. Then it went out.

Ruby sat in her web. The rain was gone too. She was alone. She was still.

stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Five legs Ruby had, and one raindrop she loved. It sat on her web like a tiny glass bead. Ruby wanted to keep it safe all night.

The wind came. The bead slid. Ruby ran to catch it, but her web shook and the drop fell into the snow.

Ruby was sad. She looked down at the cold white yard.

Then she saw a light. It was small and far away, across the snowy yard. It was the color of new leaves. It did not move. It just stayed there, past the fence, past the trees.

Ruby climbed down. She tried to brush the snow away. She tried to dig with her legs. The snow was too deep.

A kind wind blew warm air. The snow turned to water. A new drop made a home on Ruby's web.

But Ruby did not look at it. She looked across the yard, where the small green light still shone.

She reached out one leg. She could not touch it. She never could.

The sun went down. The light stayed on. Ruby stayed too.

stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Fuzzy little Ruby was a spider. She lived in a web by the window. One cold day, a raindrop got stuck in her web. It shone like a tiny glass ball. Ruby wanted to keep it. But the sun was going down, and the air grew cold. The drop would freeze.

Ruby tried to brush it free with one leg. It would not move. She tried to dig at it with her tiny feet. It held on tight. She wrapped it in a bit of warm silk from her belly. That helped a little. The drop stopped shaking.

Then Ruby saw a light. It was far across the snowy yard. A small glow, like a little sun left on the ground. It blinked and blinked. Ruby forgot the drop. She forgot the cold. She walked to the edge of her web. She reached one leg out. The light was so far. She reached and reached.

The drop slipped from her web and fell into the snow. Ruby did not see. She only saw the light. She reached for it until the sky went dark. The light stayed where it was. Ruby never got there.

stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Fuzzy little Ruby was a spider. She lived in a bush by the window. One day a raindrop fell on her web. It was cold and heavy. Ruby had a little problem. The raindrop pulled her web down.

Ruby did not like that. She wanted to fix it. She tried to brush the water away. She tried to dig her feet in. But the web was too wet. She felt sad.

Then the sun came out. It was warm. The raindrop got small. Ruby fixed her web. She was happy.

But then she saw it. Across the snowy yard, a little light was on. It was green and soft. It was far away. Ruby looked and looked. She wanted to go there. She wanted to touch it.

The light did not move. Ruby reached out. She reached and reached. The light stayed far. The snow was cold. Ruby was small. She kept looking at the light. She kept reaching. The light was always there. She could not get it. She never got it.

stories.name: Wren

axes.where: at the end of a long road

stories.text:
Mittens on, Wren went out to see the spider. The spider lived in the corner of the fence. Its web was thin and white. A round raindrop sat in the middle.

"Hello, spider," said Wren.

The raindrop wobbled. The spider did not move.

Snow began to fall. Flakes landed on the web. The raindrop grew cold. It shivered. Then it fell.

Wren tried to catch it in her mitten. She missed. The drop hit the snow and was gone.

"Oops," said Wren.

The spider ran in a circle. It looked funny. Wren laughed. Then she felt sad. The spider wanted the drop back. It ran and ran.

Wren looked down the long road. Far away, at the end, a small green light blinked. It was pretty. She reached out her hand. But she could not touch it. It was too far.

She picked up her mitten and went home. The spider stayed on the web. It waited for a new drop. The light blinked on. Wren could not carry it home.

stories.name: Wren

axes.where: at the end of a long road

stories.text:
Mia the spider lived in a big oak tree. One cold day, a raindrop fell on her web. It was round and shiny. Mia wanted to keep it. She tried to carry it to her nest. But the drop slipped and popped on her head. She laughed. That was funny.

Then snow came. The raindrop turned to ice. Mia was sad. She pulled on her tiny mitten. She wanted the drop back. She looked down the long road. At the end of the road, a small green light glowed. It was far away. Mia wished she could hold it. But the light was too far.

She sat in her web. The snow fell soft and white. Mia thought of the round drop. She thought of the green light. She could not have either one. Her mitten was cold. The road was long. The light stayed far away. Mia was sad. She stayed in her web and waited.

stories.name: Wren

axes.where: at the end of a long road

stories.text:
Mittens off, Wren found a spider in the snow. The spider sat on a raindrop frozen round and clear. "You are a little glass ball," Wren said. The spider did not answer. It was too cold to talk.

Wren tried to carry the raindrop home. It slipped. It rolled. It went plop into a snowbank. Wren laughed, then felt sad. The spider waved one thin leg. That was funny and also not funny.

Wren looked down the long road. At the end of the road, a small green light was glowing. It was far away. It shone through the falling snow.

"I want to go there," Wren said. "I want to hold it."

Wren walked and walked. The green light stayed far. It did not get bigger. It did not get closer.

The spider climbed onto Wren's mitten. The raindrop was gone. The snow kept falling.

At the end of the long road, the green light blinked once. Then it went out. Wren stood still in the white snow. The spider was still there. But the light was not.

stories.name: Wren

axes.where: at the end of a long road

stories.text:
Mia the spider sat in her web. She wanted a raindrop. One cold day, snow fell instead. Wren put on a red mitten. She saw Mia on a branch. "Silly spider," Wren said. "Rain is gone. Snow is here." Mia did not care. She held out her round legs.

Then Wren saw a green light. It was far away, at the end of a long road. The light glowed through the snow. Wren forgot Mia. She forgot the snow. She wanted that light. "I must go," Wren said. She tried to carry Mia with her. But Mia was too small. Wren laughed. "You are a snow spider now!"

Mia still wanted her raindrop. Wren still wanted her light. The light never came closer. The road was too long. The snow grew deep. Wren sat down. She cried a little. Mia sat beside her. No raindrop came. No light came. The green light just blinked, far and cold, at the end of the long road. Wren could not reach it. Not ever.

stories.name: Wren

axes.where: at the end of a long road

stories.text:
Mia the spider sat on her web. She wanted a raindrop. One big round drop fell. It plopped on her head. She laughed. That was funny.

Then she saw it. Far away, at the end of a long road, a small green light glowed. Mia forgot the raindrop.

She wanted the light. She wanted the light. She wanted the light.

She put on a mitten. She tried to carry her web. The snow came down. It was a snowy day. Her web got heavy. She could not carry it.

"I want the light," she said. "I want the light."

She walked and walked. The snow got deep. Her mitten fell off. She did not care. She only saw the light.

At last she came close. The light was just a lamp on a pole. It was cold and far. She could not touch it.

Mia sat in the snow. She was small. She was tired. She had no web. She had no drop.

"I want the light," she said. "I want the light."

But the light did not want her. The snow covered her. And she was sad.

stories.name: Jay

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text: In the garden, Jay watched a spider spin a web between two red flowers. The morning was windy. A fat raindrop hung on the web and shook in the breeze. "It will fall," Jay said. His friend May sat on a boot nearby. "Help me build a wall," she said. They piled small stones around the flowers. The wind blew hard. The raindrop danced and did not fall. Jay felt calm. He looked down the street. Far away, on a car, a small green light glowed. He wanted it. He reached out, but his hand touched only wind. May pulled him back to the web. "Look," she said. The spider was safe. The raindrop held on. Jay smiled. The little light stayed far away, but his friend was here, and the web was bright with sun.

stories.name: Jay

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
I saw a spider on the window. Jay saw it too. "Look," said Jay. "A little spider."

The spider sat on a raindrop. The raindrop was big and round. The wind blew hard. It was a windy morning.

The raindrop shook. The spider held on tight. Jay held on to his boot. "Don't fall," Jay said.

Then Jay saw a light. It was on a car far down the street. The light was small and green. It blinked in the wind. Jay wanted to touch it. He could not.

"Help me," said Jay. His friend May came. "Watch the spider," she said. "That is your job."

Jay watched the spider. The green light blinked. Jay turned back to the spider. The wind grew calm. The raindrop slid down slow. The spider rode it safe to the ground.

Jay smiled. "You did it," he said. The green light blinked far away. Jay did not need it. He had the spider and his friend.

stories.name: Jay

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
I saw a spider on a raindrop. The drop hung from a leaf. The spider was small and black. It held on with tiny legs. The wind blew hard. Jay put on his boot. He ran to the yard.

"Come see," said Jay. His friend May came. She did not shake. She was calm. "The spider is safe," she said.

Jay looked down the street. A car sat far away. A light was on it. A soft green light. It glowed and glowed. Jay wanted to touch it. He took a step. Then he stopped. The light was too far. He turned back to the drop.

The wind blew again. The drop fell. The spider landed on a leaf. It was okay. Jay smiled. May smiled too. They watched the spider climb.

Jay looked down the street one more time. The green light still shone. He could not reach it. But he did not need to. The spider was safe. That was enough. The wind was strong. But Jay felt warm and happy.

stories.name: Jay

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text: I found a spider in my boot. Jay shook his boot, and the spider fell out. It was tiny and black. It crawled to a leaf. A raindrop hit the leaf. The spider held on. Jay smiled. Then he saw it. A small green light on a car far down the street. It glowed. Jay wanted that light. He forgot the spider. He walked toward the light. His friend May came. "Come see the spider," she said. Jay did not hear. "I want that light," he said. He said it again. "I want that light. I want that light." The wind blew hard. Jay's boot got wet. May took his hand. "The light is just a car," she said. "Look here." She showed him the spider. The spider sat calm on the leaf. The raindrop fell. The spider did not fall. Jay blinked. The light was far away. It was just a light. He sat with May. They watched the spider. It was safe. Jay felt calm too. Then the wind stopped. The sun came out.

stories.name: Jay

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text:
In the corner of the window, Jay watched a spider. The spider sat on its web. A raindrop hung on a leaf. Jay liked the spider. He liked the drop.

Then Jay saw the light. It was far down the street, on a car. A small light, green and bright. It was on. It was off. It was on.

"Come and see the spider," said his friend May.

"I want that light," said Jay.

He put on his boot. The wind blew. He did not shake. He was not calm.

"I want that light. I want that light."

May took his hand. "The light is far. Look here."

The raindrop fell. The spider climbed. May helped Jay build a little home for the spider in a jar.

The wind went soft. Jay felt calm. He did not need the far light. He had the spider, the drop, and May.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: in the sky, very low
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text: Spiders spin webs in the early morning. Cleo is a small spider. She spins her web between two flowers. A fat raindrop hangs on a leaf. It shines like a tiny glass ball. Cleo wants that raindrop. She wants to brush it with her feet. She wants to swim in it. Her friend Pip is a jolly beetle. Pip says, "That drop is too big for you." Cleo tries to grab it. The drop shakes and falls. It lands on a thirsty ant. The ant drinks and thanks the sky. Cleo feels sad. Then she sees a new drop. It is smaller and just right. She steps on it and laughs. Far away, low in the sky, a small green light glows. Cleo looks at it for a moment. It is pretty. Then she turns back to her web.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: in the sky, very low
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text: Spiders spin webs in the early morning. Cleo the spider spun hers between two wet leaves. She worked hard. Her web was thin and silver. Then a raindrop fell and sat right in the middle. It was round and shiny. "I will brush it away," said Cleo. But the raindrop held on. Her friend Bumble the bee flew by. "Let me help," said Bumble. He tried to swim through the web and shook it. The raindrop wobbled but stayed. Cleo looked up. Low in the sky sat a small light, pale and far. It blinked once. She wanted to reach it. She wished she could hold it in her legs. But the light was too high, and her web was too low. "You are jolly good at webs," said Bumble. "Forget the drop." Cleo turned back. Then she saw the raindrop had a tiny spider inside, waving. It was her baby sister! Cleo laughed. The low light twinkled, but Cleo did not need it now. She had her sister safe in the drop.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: in the sky, very low
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Spiders do not like the rain. Cleo the spider sat in her web and watched big clouds roll in. She needed to brush her web clean before the storm.

A raindrop landed on a leaf. It was round and bright. Cleo wanted it. She wanted to swim in it. She reached out one leg.

In the sky, very low, a small light glowed. It was green. It blinked in the early morning. Cleo turned toward it. She forgot the raindrop.

Her friend Ben the beetle came by. "You look sad," he said.

"I want that light," said Cleo. "It is so jolly and bright."

"You cannot reach the sky," said Ben.

The raindrop slid off the leaf. It fell into a puddle. The puddle caught the green light. The light was right there. Cleo laughed. She did not need the sky after all.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: in the sky, very low
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Six tiny feet woke Cleo the spider. Rain was coming. She had to fix her web before the drops fell. She worked fast, leg by leg. A raindrop landed on her thread. It shone like a bead.

Then she saw it. Low in the early morning sky, a small light glowed. It was far away and green. Cleo wanted it. She reached a leg toward it. She could not touch it.

Her friend Bea the beetle came by. "Your web is torn," Bea said.

"I want that light," Cleo said. She reached again. "I want it. I want it."

"You can't have it," Bea said. "But you can have this." Bea gave her a wet leaf to brush the dust off.

Cleo looked at the light. She reached once more. Then she sighed. She went back to her web.

The twist came when the sun rose. The light was just a leaf, jolly and green, stuck on a branch. Cleo laughed. She did not want to swim to it after all. She stayed home, warm and dry.

stories.name: Cleo

axes.where: in the sky, very low
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Six tiny feet tapped on the web. Cleo the spider woke up. She was hungry. A fat raindrop hung on a leaf.

Cleo wanted that raindrop. She wanted to brush it with her feet. She wanted to swim in it. "Oh, so jolly," she said.

Then she saw the light. A small green light sat low in the sky, near the hills. It was far away. It was so pretty. "I want it," said Cleo. "I want it."

Her friend Bee buzzed by. "That is just a lamp on a porch," said Bee.

"I want it," said Cleo. "I want it. I want it."

Cleo left the raindrop. She climbed down. She walked and walked. The light stayed far. The sun came up. The light went out.

Cleo sat on a stone. Bee came with a leaf. On the leaf was the raindrop. It shone like a little lamp. "Oh," said Cleo. "It was here all along."

stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in a garden next door
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Fog wrapped the garden like a soft gray blanket. Sid the spider sat in his web between two wet leaves. He waited for a raindrop. One drop would be his supper. He did not want a fly. He wanted a raindrop, round and cold and clean.

The night was slow. Sid held still. He counted the drips on the roof. He used a bent spoon to catch one, but it slipped away.

Next door, past the fence, a small light glowed in the fog. It was green. Sid saw it once. It looked like a tiny faraway leaf. He wished he could put it in his web. He reached one leg toward it. The fence was too far. He turned back to his raindrop.

He tried to bake a plan in his head. Wait. Catch. Hold. But no drop came. The fog grew thick. The green light stayed far away.

Then a drop fell. It landed on a stone, not his web. Sid crawled down. The stone was dry. The drop was gone. The light blinked once, then went out. Sid sat in the dark, still hungry.

stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in a garden next door
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text: Fog sat on the garden like a soft wet blanket. Sid the spider lived in a rose bush. One big raindrop hung on a leaf. It was round and clear. Sid wanted it. "Come here, little drop," said Sid. He reached out two thin legs. The drop did not move. Sid went slow. He used a tiny spoon of silk to pull it close. He wanted to bake it into his web. But drop was too heavy. Then Sid saw a light in the garden next door. It glowed small and green. It looked warm. It looked kind. Sid reached for it. He reached and reached. His legs were too short. The green light stayed far away. Sid looked back at his drop. It was gone. It fell on the grass. The fog got thicker. The green light blinked once. Then it went out. Sid sat alone in the dark. No drop. No light. Just wet, cold leaves.

stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in a garden next door
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Fog wrapped the garden like a wet blanket. Sid the spider sat on his web. A raindrop hung on a silky thread. It was round and cold and shiny.

Sid wanted to keep the drop. He held it with two thin legs. He watched it wobble. It made his web feel heavy and slow.

Next door, past the fence, a small light glowed in the fog. It was pale and far away. Sid turned toward it. He reached a leg out. He could not touch it.

He let go of the drop. He climbed to the fence. The light stayed far. He reached and reached. His legs shook. He wanted it so much.

He forgot his web. He forgot the drop. He forgot to bake in the warm sun. He forgot his little spoon of dew.

The fog grew thick. The light blinked out. Sid fell to the cold grass. He curled up small. He never found his way home.

stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in a garden next door
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Fog wrapped the garden like a wet blanket. Sid the spider sat on his web and watched a raindrop slide down a leaf. The drop was round and slow. It made the leaf bend. Sid wanted to touch it.

Then he saw the light. It was in the garden next door. A small green light, far away. It glowed through the fog.

Sid forgot the raindrop. He crawled to the edge of his web. The green light called him. He reached one thin leg toward it. He could not reach.

The raindrop fell and was gone. Sid did not care. He only wanted the light. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it.

His mother brought him a fly on a spoon. "Bake it in the sun," she said. But there was no sun. Only fog. Only the green light.

Sid left his web. He walked and walked. The light stayed far away.

At dawn, the fog lifted. The light was just a lamp on a porch. It clicked off. Sid sat in the wet grass, cold and small, too far from home.

stories.name: Sid

axes.where: in a garden next door
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Fog wrapped the garden like a soft gray blanket. Sid the spider sat on his web. He watched a raindrop slide down a leaf. It wobbled and shone. "Come here," Sid whispered. "Be mine." The drop slipped away. Sid rushed to catch it with his spoon. He wanted to keep it safe.

Then he saw the light. It was in the garden next door. A small green glow, far away. It blinked through the fog. Sid forgot the drop. "I want that light," he said. "I want that light."

He crawled fast, then slow. He forgot to bake his flies. He forgot the raindrop. "I want that light. I want that light."

The fog grew thick. The light stayed far. Sid reached out his legs. He could not touch it.

In the morning, the fog was gone. The light was gone too. It was only a jar of fireflies. They had flown away. Sid sat alone on a wet leaf. His raindrop was gone. His web was broken. He had nothing at all.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: in the window of an old house
features: a little problem that gets solved
a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Gently, Ruby looked at the dream puppy in her book. It had soft ears and a happy tail. She wanted a puppy so much. But her mom said, "Not yet."

Ruby went outside to build a snowman. Snow fell on her red mitten. She rolled a big ball. Then she rolled a small ball. Her hands got cold.

She looked up. A soft light shone in the window of the old house next door. It was green and shiny. Ruby wanted to touch it. But the window was far away. She could not reach it.

She sighed and went back to her snowman. She gave it two stick arms. Then she had an idea. She used her mitten for a hat. The snowman looked silly. Ruby laughed.

Her mom came out. "That is a fine snowman," she said. "And look." She held a small box. Inside was a toy puppy. It was soft and brown. Ruby hugged it tight.

The green light blinked once. Ruby did not mind. She had her puppy now.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: in the window of an old house
features: a little problem that gets solved
a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Greta the snow fell all day. Ruby sat by the window and wished for a puppy. She had wished for one all winter.

Ruby put on her red mitten and went outside. She wanted to build a snow dog. She rolled a big ball for the body. She rolled a small ball for the head.

Then she saw it. Down the street, in the window of an old house, a small green light was glowing. It looked like a tiny star. Ruby wanted to hold it. She reached out, but her hand only found cold air.

She built her snow dog. She gave it a shiny stone for a nose. It was good, but it was not warm. It could not lick her hand.

Ruby felt sad. Then the old house door opened. A lady came out with a real puppy. The puppy ran to Ruby and licked her mitten.

"You can keep him," said the lady. "He needs a friend."

Ruby hugged the puppy. She looked back at the window. The green light was gone. But Ruby did not mind. She had something warm at last.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: in the window of an old house
features: a little problem that gets solved
a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Gently, Ruby wanted a puppy. She drew one in the snow with her boot. She drew a tail and two round ears.

Ruby pulled her red mitten on. She wanted to build a snow puppy too. She rolled a big ball for the body. She rolled a small ball for the head.

Then she saw it. In the window of the old house, a small green light. It glowed and glowed. Ruby stopped. Her snow puppy could wait. She looked at the light. It was so shiny and far away.

She stacked the snow head on the body. But she kept turning back to the light. The light seemed to say, come here. Ruby whispered, I want to hold you, little light. Then she made two snow ears. She looked back at the light. Then she made a snow tail.

Her snow puppy was small and cold. It had no warm nose. Ruby felt sad. Then a real puppy ran out of the old house. It licked her mitten. The twist was that the green light was not far at all. It was a night light for a new puppy. Ruby hugged him. The light glowed, but now she did not need to reach it.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ruby

axes.where: in the window of an old house
features: a little problem that gets solved
a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Greta Ruby wanted a puppy. She drew a puppy in the snow with her mitten. She wanted to build a snow puppy too. But the snow was too soft. It fell down flat. Ruby felt sad.

Then she saw a light. It was in the window of an old house. The light was small and green and shiny. Ruby wanted to touch it. She wanted it to be hers. She walked to the house.

"Can I have that green light?" she asked. No one came. The light just glowed.

Ruby forgot her snow puppy. She only thought of the green light. "I want it," she said. "I want it. I want it."

A little boy opened the door. "That is a lamp," he said. "My grandma's lamp."

Ruby blinked. Then she saw a real puppy by his feet. It was small and warm.

"The lamp stays," said the boy. "But the puppy needs a friend. Do you want to play?"

Ruby looked back at the light once. Then she said yes.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ruby

features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Ginger snow fell all day. Ruby wanted a puppy. She drew one in the frost on the glass. She named him Pip.

Then Ruby saw the light. A small green light, in the window of the old house.

Ruby pulled on her mitten. She walked to the light. She wanted it. She wanted it so much.

"Pip," she said. "Pip. Pip."

She tried to build a snow puppy. The snow was too soft. It fell down.

"Pip. Pip. Pip," she said.

She looked at the green light. It was so shiny. It was so far. She could not have it.

Her mitten slipped off in the snow. Ruby sat down and cried.

Then something small and warm licked her hand. A real puppy! It was lost and cold.

Ruby picked it up. The green light blinked once, like a tiny wink. The old house was empty. Nobody lived there.

Ruby took the puppy home. She named him Pip. The green light stayed in the window, far away. Ruby did not need it now. She had Pip.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: behind the hedge
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: Winter came, and Anya wanted a puppy. She drew one with a black button nose. She taped the drawing to the wall. "I will listen for a puppy," she said. Her mom said no dogs. Anya felt sad. Then a little problem came. Her red boots had no laces. She sat in the snow and could not tie them. She found a shiny string in her pocket and fixed them. She stood up, happy. Then she saw something move behind the hedge. It was small and white. A puppy! She ran to it. But it ran away. It was not hers. It was just snow on a bush. Anya went inside. She looked at her drawing. Her boots were fixed, but her heart still wanted a puppy.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: behind the hedge
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
When Anya played in the snow, she wanted a puppy. She drew one in the snow with her boot. She gave it a name. She called it Pip.

Anya told her mom, "I want a puppy." Mom said, "Not now, Anya." Anya felt sad. She sat by the window and watched the snow fall.

Then she heard a small sound. It came from behind the hedge. She ran to listen. A little puppy was stuck in the snow. It had a shiny collar. It had a round button on its collar. Anya helped the puppy out.

"Pip!" she said. The puppy licked her hand. Anya was so happy. She ran to show Mom. But the puppy had a home. A man came and said, "Thank you." He took the puppy away.

Anya stood by the hedge. Far off, she saw a small light. It was green and soft. It blinked in the snow. She could not go to it. She could not have a puppy. She watched the light until it went out.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: behind the hedge
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
When the snow came, Anya wished for a puppy. She wished it while she buttoned her coat. She wished it while she pulled on her boots. A puppy would sit by her feet and listen to her sing.

Anya made a small dog from snow. She gave it a shiny stone for a nose. It did not bark. It did not run. The snow dog just sat and got cold.

A little problem came. Anya lost her red mitten in the snow. She looked by the tree. She looked by the step. Then she saw a glow behind the hedge. It was far away and low, a small light that stayed and stayed.

She forgot the mitten. She walked to the hedge. The light was always one step past her hands. It never came closer.

Her mitten was gone. Her snow dog melted. Anya sat down in the white yard. She could still see the soft glow behind the hedge. She wanted it so much. She wanted it so much. She wanted it so much.

The snow kept falling. The light did not come. Anya went inside alone.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: behind the hedge
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
When Anya woke up, she wanted a puppy. She sat by the window and watched the snow come down. A puppy could sit with her. A puppy could lick her hand.

Anya found a shiny button on her coat. She held it and made a wish for a puppy. Then she went outside to play in the snow.

Behind the hedge, a soft light glowed. It was small and bright and green. Anya wanted to touch it. She wanted to hold it. Maybe the light was a puppy. Maybe it was a warm little puppy waiting for her.

She pushed through the snow. She reached the hedge. The light stayed behind it, far away and close.

"Come here," she said. "Please."

She said it again. "Please. Please."

Her mittens got wet. She could not reach the light. Then the light went out.

Anya went inside. She lost her shiny button in the snow. Her hands were cold. She sat by the window and did not listen to her mother. She had no puppy. She wanted the light behind the hedge. She wanted it. She wanted it.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Anya

axes.where: behind the hedge
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: When Anya made a snow puppy, she gave it a button for a nose. She wanted a real puppy. She wanted one very much. But the puppy was only snow. It did not run. It did not listen. Then Anya saw a shiny light behind the hedge. It was small and green. It blinked in the snow. “Come here,” Anya said. The light stayed behind the hedge. “Come here,” Anya said again. “Come here, come here.” She forgot her snow puppy. She forgot the button nose. She walked to the hedge. The light was still far. It was always far. Her mittens got wet. Her toes got cold. She said “Come here” until her voice was small. The snow puppy tipped over. Its button fell in the snow. Anya did not fix it. She just looked at the little light. It was so close. It was never close. The snow kept falling. The light kept blinking. Anya sat down in the cold and said “Come here” one more time. Nobody came.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ivy

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Ivy slept, she dreamed of a puppy. A small brown puppy with one floppy ear. In her dream, the puppy licked her nose. She giggled and woke up.

The room was dark. Snow tapped the window. Ivy tiptoed to look outside. The yard was white and quiet. Her boots were icy by the door.

Then she saw it. Far across the snowy yard, past the fence, a tiny light blinked. It was small and green. It looked like a frog sitting on a rock. Ivy wanted to hold it.

She put on her boots. They went squish. She opened the door. A cold wind said brrr. She took one step. Her foot made a deep hole. She fell in the snow. Her boots stuck up like two black sticks.

"Help," she said. "I am a snow girl."

Mom came and pulled her out. They laughed so loud the snow seemed to shake.

Ivy looked across the yard again. The little light was still there. She could not touch it. She could not make it hers. But she did not drop her smile. She waved goodnight to it.

Then she went back to bed. She dreamed of the puppy again.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ivy

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Ivy slept, she dreamed of a puppy. It was small and warm and soft. She named it Flip. In her dream, Flip licked her nose. She giggled in her sleep.

Outside, snow fell. Late at night, the moon was high. Ivy woke up. Her room was dark and cold. She looked out the window. Across the snowy yard, a light shone. It was small and green. It blinked like a slow firefly.

Ivy wished she could hold it. She wished she could hold Flip. The light was too far. The snow was deep. She pressed her hand on the icy glass.

A frog hopped by the fence. It slipped on a patch of ice. It did a funny flip. Ivy laughed. Then she looked back at the green light. It was still there.

“I want you,” she whispered. She did not mean the frog. She did not mean the light. She wanted her puppy.

A snowflake made a soft drop on the sill. Ivy yawned. She went back to bed. In her dream, Flip was waiting.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ivy

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Ivy slept, she dreamed of a puppy. It was small and soft and had one floppy ear. She named him Waffles in the dream. Every night, Waffles ran to her and licked her nose.

Ivy wanted a real Waffles. She drew him on paper. She told her mom. Her mom said, "Maybe one day."

Late at night, Ivy woke up. She walked to the window. Across the snowy yard, she saw a little light. It glowed by the fence. It was not a star. It was not a lamp. It was just a small warm dot that made her chest feel funny.

"Oh," Ivy said. "Is that Waffles?"

The light did not move. It never moved. She pressed her hand on the icy glass. A frog sat on the sill outside and blinked at her. Ivy laughed. "You are not a puppy," she said.

She saw one drop of water slide down the window. Then she climbed back to bed. She looked at the light one more time. It stayed far away.

In the morning, Ivy still wanted Waffles. But that night, she knew the little light was waiting. It was always there. She could see it. She could not reach it. That was okay. She would keep looking.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ivy

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Ivy slept, she dreamed of a puppy. It was small and warm. It had soft ears. She wanted to hold it.

Late at night, she woke up. Her room was dark. Out the window, snow covered the yard. Across the snowy yard, a little light glowed. It was green and far away.

Ivy sat up. The puppy was gone. She looked at the light. "I want my puppy," she said. She said it again. "I want my puppy."

She put her feet on the icy floor. She thought of the puppy's wet nose. She thought of its tail. She did not think of the light, but she saw it. It blinked like a small frog in the snow.

"Please," she whispered. "Please, puppy."

Then she heard a funny sound. A drop of water fell from the roof. Plop. It landed on her nose. Ivy laughed.

She climbed back into bed. The light stayed across the yard. She closed her eyes. "I want my puppy," she said. She said it until she slept.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Ivy

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
Curled up in bed, Ivy hugged her toy dog and wished for a real puppy. Late at night, she tiptoed to the window. Across the snowy yard, a little light glowed. It was small and far away. It looked like a tiny golden puppy.

Ivy pressed her nose to the icy glass. "Puppy," she whispered. "Come here, puppy."

The light did not move. It just stayed there, soft and bright.

"Puppy," she said again. "Puppy, puppy, puppy."

A frog on the windowsill went croak. Ivy giggled, but only for a second. She looked back at the light. Her want felt like a big drop of water in her chest. It went splash, splash, splash.

She pulled on her boots. The snow was deep. She took one step. Then two. The light stayed far away.

"Puppy," she said. "Puppy, puppy, puppy."

Her mama found her at the door and carried her back to bed. Through the window, the little light still shone. Ivy closed her eyes. "Puppy," she whispered. "Puppy, puppy, puppy."

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Joon

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Joon woke up, she wanted a puppy. She wanted a soft puppy with warm ears. She told her mom at breakfast. Mom said, "Maybe one day." Joon ate her cake and did not feel happy.

That evening the air turned cold. Joon put on her coat and went outside. The yard was white with early snow. She saw a small light far across the snowy yard. It was green and it blinked. Joon stood still. She did not know why, but she wanted to walk to it. She took one step. Then she stopped.

"Count to ten," she said. She counted. One, two, three. The green light made her feel dizzy and warm. Then it went away.

Joon went back inside. She felt sleepy. In the morning, a small puppy sat by the door. It had warm ears. "For you," said Mom. Joon held the puppy close. The green light was gone, but she did not need it now.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Joon

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Joon wished for a puppy, she wished hard. She wished on stars and on her birthday cake. She wished at bedtime. Her mom said, "A puppy is a big job." Joon said, "I can do big jobs."

That evening was cold. Joon put on her coat. She went outside. The yard was white with snow. She could see her breath.

Across the snowy yard, a small light blinked. It was green and low. It looked like a tiny eye. Joon took one step. Then two. Her boots made soft sounds. The light did not come closer.

"Come here," Joon said. The light stayed far away.

She tried to count her steps. One, two, three. She got dizzy in the cold. She stopped. The green light just blinked and blinked.

Joon went inside. She felt sad. Then she heard a small sound at the door. A puppy! It was small and warm. It had been lost in the snow.

Joon hugged it. The light was gone. But the puppy was here. That was better.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Joon

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Joon wished for a puppy, she wished hard. She wished on stars and on candles. She wished on her birthday cake. She wanted a small dog to hug. Her mom said, "Not yet." Her dad said, "Maybe soon." Joon would count the days.

One cold autumn evening, she stood at the window. Across the snowy yard, a small light blinked. It was green and soft. It looked like a puppy's eye. Joon put on her coat and ran out. The light danced away. It made her dizzy. She reached and reached. Her hands found only cold air. Night after night, the light came back. Joon wanted to hold it. She wanted it to be hers.

Then her mom called her inside. On the floor sat a warm little puppy. It had a green collar. Joon held it close. The light was gone. She did not need to count anymore.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Joon

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Joon got home, she drew a puppy on paper. She gave it big ears. She gave it a soft nose. She named it Mochi. Every night she said good night to the paper. Every morning she said good morning to the paper. Her mom said, maybe one day. Joon said, maybe now.

Then she saw the little green light. It was across the snowy yard. It was small and far. It sat by the old fence. It did not move. It only glowed, slow and soft. Joon put on her coat. She walked to the fence. The light stayed far. She walked more. The light stayed far. Her boots got cold. Her hands got cold.

At home she ate cake for her birthday. She tried to count her candles. One, two, three. The room went dizzy. She closed her eyes. She saw the light.

She went out again and again. Snow on her hat. Snow on her nose. The light was a small green star she could not hold.

Then one night the light came closer. It was a puppy. A small puppy with big ears. It had a soft nose. It walked to her feet. It was warm.

Joon did not count. She did not feel dizzy. She held the puppy and laughed. The puppy licked her cheek. Her wish was home.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Joon

axes.where: across the snowy yard

stories.text:
When Joon closed her eyes, she saw a puppy. It was small and soft and hers. She wanted to feed it cake. She wanted to count its toes.

The evening was cold. Joon stood at the window. Across the snowy yard, a little light glowed. It was small and green. It blinked like a slow star.

Joon put her hand on the glass. "Come here," she said. The light did not come. It only blinked. She felt dizzy with wanting.

She said it again. "Come here. Come here." The light stayed far away. It was always far away. It blinked and blinked.

Joon's mama called her to supper. Joon did not turn. "Come here," she said. The words were warm and tired. The light was cold and far.

Then the door opened. A small puppy ran in. It was soft and real. It licked her hand.

Joon laughed. She held it close. The green light blinked once more, then went out. She did not need it now.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Zoe

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Gently, Zoe wished for a puppy. She wished at breakfast. She wished at lunch. She wished on every star.

One warm evening, she sat by the pond. The sky turned rosy. She found a long stick. She gave the water a tap, tap, tap.

Deep down, something glowed. A small green light. It was far away and cool. Zoe leaned over. She wanted it. She reached with her stick. The light stayed deep. It would not come.

"Come here, little light," she said. The light just shone. It was like a tiny moon under the water. She could not hold it. She could not keep it.

Then the water wiggled. A wet nose popped up. A puppy! It shook and splashed her. She laughed. Her dream came true.

But the green light still glowed deep down. Zoe looked at it once more. She gave a little wave. Then she ran home with her new friend.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Zoe

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Good night, Zoe. She wanted a puppy more than anything. She drew puppies on paper. She dreamed of a warm, wiggly puppy to hug.

At sunset, she sat by the pond. The water was still. Deep down, she saw a small green light. It glowed like a tiny star under the water. She wanted it. She reached with a stick, but it was too far.

She came back the next day. She gave the water a soft tap. The light came back. It always came back at sunset. Her cheeks turned rosy. She reached and reached. She could not touch it.

One evening, a funny thing happened. A frog jumped on her foot. She laughed so hard she almost fell in.

Then came the twist. The green light was not a puppy at all. It was just a shiny bottle. But when she looked up, a real puppy licked her hand. It had followed her home.

She still watched the light at sunset. She held her puppy close. Some lights you reach for. Some love just finds you.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Zoe

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Good dreams came to Zoe every night. She wished for a puppy. A soft, small puppy to lick her hand.

At sunset, Zoe sat by the pond. She had a stick. She would tap the water. Tap, tap, tap.

Then she saw the light. It was deep at the bottom of the pond. A small green light. It glowed like a tiny moon.

"Come here, puppy," Zoe said to the light. She thought the light was a puppy. She reached in. The water was cold. She could not touch it.

Every night she came back. Tap, tap, tap. The light stayed deep. It never came up. Her cheeks turned rosy from the wind. Her heart felt heavy.

One night she leaned too far. Splash! She got all wet. A frog jumped on her head. "Ribbit," said the frog. Zoe laughed. That was funny.

Then the light blinked. It was not a puppy at all. It was a firefly. It lived in the pond and could never leave.

Zoe went home. She still wanted a puppy. But she knew the light would always be too far to hold.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Zoe

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Good dreams came to Zoe at night. She dreamed of a puppy every single time. A small brown puppy with one floppy ear. He slept on her feet and licked her nose.

At sunset, she sat by the pond. The water was still. Deep down, a small green light glowed. It shimmered like a tiny star.

"Oh," Zoe whispered. "Is that you, puppy?"

She found a stick and gave the water a tap. The light bobbed. It did not come up. It just kept glowing, far and deep, where her hand could never go.

The sky turned rosy. Zoe leaned close. The light looked like two puppy eyes, waiting.

"Come here," she said. "Please come here."

The light only sank lower.

Then something funny happened. A frog jumped on her head. It sat there like a hat. Zoe laughed so hard she almost fell in.

That was the twist. The frog was not a frog. It was the puppy, wet and wiggly! He had been swimming the whole time.

Zoe hugged him. But at night, she still dreamed of the light, deep in the pond, glowing and glowing. She reached for it. She always reached.

stories.topic: a girl and her dream puppy
stories.name: Zoe

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text: Gone was the day Zoe got her dream puppy. She wished for a soft pup. A pup to nap with. A pup to run with. At sunset she saw a green light deep at the bottom of the pond. She wanted it. She reached for it. Her hand got wet. She poked the water with a stick. The light did not come. "Come here," she said. She said it again. "Come here. Come here. Come here." A frog went plop. It made a funny sound. Zoe laughed a little. Then she looked back at the green light. She did a small tap on the water. The light stayed far and low. A rosy glow covered the sky. Zoe wished the light could be her pup. But wishing is not having. She sat very still. The light just shook. The twist was this: the light was only the sun's last gleam. Still Zoe reached. "Come here. Come here." She reached and reached and reached.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Beth

axes.where: at the end of a long road
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: A rabbit can make a knee feel better. Beth knew this was true. She sat on the front step and held her scraped knee. The skin was red and round and sore. Her rabbit, Pip, sat beside her. He did not fix knees. He only wiggled his nose. Beth wanted to run and play. But her knee said no. Mom came out with a soft cloth. She cleaned the scrape. It stung. Beth did not cry. She held Pip tight. Then she saw it. Way down the long road, a tiny light blinked on. It was small and green and far away. Like a lost star. The moon was up too, big and white. Beth wanted to grab that little light. But it was too far. Mom put a bandage on her knee. It had stars on it. Now Beth could stand. She could walk. The little light still blinked at the end of the road. Beth waved goodnight to it. Then she went inside for bed.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Beth

axes.where: at the end of a long road
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
A rabbit sat in the yard. Beth ran to grab it. Then she fell on a rock. Her knee hurt. The skin was scraped and red.

Mama cleaned it with a soft cloth. Beth sat still. She said, "Ouch."

Mama put on a round bandage. It was the color of a peach.

"All better," Mama said.

Beth looked down the long road. Something shone there. It was small and soft. It looked like a faraway lamp. It was not the moon. The moon was round and white and high.

Beth wanted to go down the road. She wanted to touch the shine.

"Not tonight," Mama said. "It is late."

The rabbit hopped back. It looked at Beth. Its nose went up and down.

Beth forgot the road for a minute. She forgot the shine for a minute.

She left a bit of apple by the fence. The rabbit came close. It ate the apple. Its whiskers moved.

Beth smiled. Her knee still hurt a little. But the rabbit was here. She said goodnight to the rabbit. She went inside.

Far down the road, the light stayed on. Beth did not go to it. Not yet.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Beth

axes.where: at the end of a long road
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
A rabbit can make a girl forget her knee. Beth was hopping home when she fell. Her knee got scraped. It stung. She sat on the grass and held it.

The moon was round and white. Just before bedtime, the road looked long. At the end of that road, far away, a little light shone. It was green and soft. Beth wanted to touch it. She did not know why.

She got up and hopped like a rabbit. Hop, hop, hop. The light stayed far away. Her knee still hurt a little.

Then her rabbit came. He had a soft cloth. He wrapped her knee. The sting went away.

"Can you grab the light?" Beth asked.

The rabbit shook his head. "We can look at it," he said.

So they sat and looked. The light blinked once. Beth felt warm. Her knee was better. She held her rabbit. The moon was round. The road was long. The little light was still there.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Beth

axes.where: at the end of a long road
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
A rabbit hopped across Beth's yard and she ran to catch it. She tripped on a root and scraped her knee. It hurt. It was a little problem.

Mom cleaned it and put on a round bandage. Beth could still feel the sting.

Then she saw the light. Far away, at the end of the long road, a soft glow waited.

"It's bedtime," Mom said.

Beth looked out her window. The moon was up. The light still called.

She tried to grab her bunny. She tried to think of her knee. But the light pulled her eyes back down the road.

"Beth," Mom said. "Story time."

Beth climbed into bed. She heard the rabbit somewhere outside. Her knee ached under the round bandage. But all she wanted was to walk that long road. All the way. To the light.

"Close your eyes," Mom said.

Beth closed them. Behind her lids the light stayed. At the end of the long road. Out of reach. Always out of reach.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Beth

axes.where: at the end of a long road
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
A rabbit can help a scraped knee. Beth sat on the step. Her knee hurt. The rabbit hopped close. She put a round bandage on it. That was the little problem. It got solved. Good.

Then she saw the light. It was small and green. It sat at the end of a long road. The moon was up. It was just before bedtime. She wanted to grab it. She could not. The light was too far. She reached. She reached.

The rabbit stayed. The light stayed. She wanted it. She wanted it. The road was long. The light was small. It was green. It was hers to see. Not hers to hold. She reached. She reached. The moon was round. The night was soft. She reached. She reached.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Mira

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Pitter-patter went the rain on the roof. Mira the rabbit ran too fast and fell. Her knee went scrape. Red drops mixed with the wet.

"Ow," said Mira. She sat on the step.

Her mom came out. "Come in, cozy one."

They put a soft cloth on her knee. Mom read a book. The rain went drum on the window. Mira did a clap with her hands when the book was done.

Then Mira looked down the street. Far away, on a car, a little light was on. It was small and green. It blinked in the rain. Mira wanted to touch it. She did not know why. It was just a light on a car.

She looked back at her book. She looked at the light again.

The car drove away. The light went with it.

Mira's knee still hurt. She went inside. The rain kept falling all night.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Mira

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Puddles jumped when Mira ran. She ran fast on the wet sidewalk. Then she fell. Her knee went scrape.

"Ow," said Mira. She held her leg.

Rain went tap tap on her hood. It made a soft drum on the roof of the car. Mira sat on the step and looked at her knee. It was red and it hurt.

Her mom came out. "Oh, sweet girl." She put a cozy blanket on Mira. They went inside.

Mira looked out the window. Far down the street, a little car sat by the curb. One small light on it stayed on. It was not red. It was not blue. It was the soft color of new leaves.

She wanted to go and see it. She wanted to touch it. But her knee hurt too much to walk.

Her mom gave her a hug. "It will feel better soon."

Mira did not clap or smile. The rain kept falling. The little light kept shining, far away.

She never got to see it up close.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Mira

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Puddles filled the road. Mira the rabbit hopped home with a scraped knee. It hurt when she moved. She sat under a big leaf to rest.

Rain went tap tap on a drum. Thunder made a loud clap. Mira wished she were cozy at home.

Then she saw it. Far down the street, on a car, a small light glowed. It was soft and green. It blinked in the rain.

Mira forgot her knee. She hopped toward the light. The rain got colder. Her knee got sorer. But the light stayed on.

She hopped and hopped. The street was long. Every time she got close, the car seemed farther away.

At last she reached the car. The light was just a sticker. A green star on the glass. It did not know her. It did not blink for her.

Mira sat down on the wet road. Her knee hurt worse now. The rain hid her tears.

She never got home that night. She just watched the little green star until the rain stopped, and then it went dark.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Mira

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Pitter-patter went the rain on the roof. Mira ran fast and fell. Her knee got a scrape. It hurt. She cried a little.

Mama put a cozy blanket on her. They sat by the window. Thunder went drum, drum. Rain went clap, clap on the glass.

Mira looked down the street. A car sat far away. On the car, a small light. It was green. It was soft and small. Mira wanted to touch it.

"Stay here," said Mama.

But Mira got up. She limped to the door. The green light pulled her. Down the wet street she went. Her knee stung.

The car was far. So far. The light did not come closer.

She got to the car at last. The green light was just a sticker. A sticker on the glass. She touched it. It was cold.

Mira sat down on the wet ground. Her knee hurt more now. The rain did not stop. The light did not glow. She was cold, and the window was dark.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Mira

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Papa said a rabbit never cries. Mira fell on the wet stones and her knee turned red. The rain went drum, drum on the roof. Mama put a cozy blanket on her and said, shh, shh.

Mira looked out the window. Down the street a car sat alone in the rain. A small green lamp was on inside it. It was soft and warm and far away.

She wanted to touch it. She wanted to hold it.

She got up. Her knee hurt. She went to the door.

The green lamp blinked, slow, slow. Come here, it said with no words.

Mira walked down the street. Rain got in her eyes. The drum was loud. She did not clap. She did not stop.

The car was cold and empty. No one was inside.

The small green lamp was just the radio, and it went dark.

Mira stood in the rain. Her knee hurt so much. No one came for her.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Jack

axes.where: at the top of the stairs
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
In the snow, Jack fell and scraped his knee. It hurt. He sat in the cold and cried.

Then he saw it. At the top of the stairs, a small green light. It blinked once. Jack wanted to touch it. He reached up. He could not get it.

His mom came outside. She gave him a hug. She put a bandage on his knee. It had a red button on it. Jack liked the button.

"Can you climb the stairs?" Mom asked.

Jack was not sure. He looked up. The green light was still there. It felt far away. He wanted it.

Jack held the rail. He went up one step. Then two. His knee hurt, but he kept going. He did not reach the light. It stayed high and small.

At the top, Jack felt proud. His knee was okay. The light blinked again. Jack waved at it. Then he went inside for cocoa.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Jack

axes.where: at the top of the stairs
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
I fell on the icy steps and scraped my knee. Jack sat in the snow and cried. Then he saw the light at the top of the stairs. It was small and green. It glowed through the falling snow.

Jack wanted to climb up and touch it. But his knee hurt too much. He held his red button in his pocket. It was his lucky button.

Mom came out and cleaned his knee. She put on a bandage. Jack felt proud of being brave.

"Can I climb the stairs now?" Jack asked.

"Not today," Mom said. "Too icy."

Jack looked up. The green light was still there. It seemed to say, come here. Jack reached one hand toward it. His fingers got only snow.

Mom carried him inside. Jack drank warm milk. He forgot the light for a while.

Then he looked out the window. The light was still at the top of the stairs. Small. Green. Far away.

Jack waved at it. It did not wave back. He closed his eyes and slept.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Jack

axes.where: at the top of the stairs
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: In the snow, Jack fell down and scraped his knee. It hurt. He sat in the cold and held his leg. Then he saw it. A small green light was at the top of the stairs. It glowed in the snow. Jack wanted to climb up and touch it. He got up. His knee hurt. But the light was so pretty. He wanted it. He could not have it. Mom came out. She put a button on his coat. She cleaned his knee. She put on a bandage. "You are brave," she said. Jack looked up. The green light was still there. It blinked once. Then it went away in the snow. Jack felt proud. He did not need the light. He went inside with Mom. They had warm soup. His knee felt better. The snow kept falling.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Jack

axes.where: at the top of the stairs
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
In the snow, Jack fell and scraped his knee. It hurt a little. He wanted to go inside. He had a button on his coat. He tried to climb the snowy stairs. Then he saw the light. A small green light at the top of the stairs. It glowed in the cold air.

Jack forgot his knee. He reached for the light. He climbed one step. The light stayed far away. He climbed more. His knee hurt, but he wanted the light. He wanted it so much.

His mom came out. She cleaned his knee. She put on a bandage. “You are brave,” she said. Jack felt proud.

He looked up. The light was still there. He reached again. He could not touch it. He never could.

His mom took his hand. They went inside. The warm room felt good. But Jack looked out the window.

The green light was still at the top of the stairs. He wanted it. He reached for it. He could not have it. He wanted it. He reached. He could not have it.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Jack

axes.where: at the top of the stairs
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
I fell on the ice and scraped my knee. Jack was sad. He wanted to run and play. But his knee hurt.

Then Jack saw the green light. It was at the top of the stairs. It was snowy and cold. The light glowed soft and far.

Jack wanted the light. He tried to climb the stairs. His knee stung. He held the rail and pulled. One step. Two steps.

The light stayed far. Jack reached. "Wait," he said. "Wait for me."

He touched his coat button. He was proud he got up. But the light was still far.

"Wait," he said. "Wait for me." He climbed. He reached.

His mom kissed his knee. She put a bandage on it.

Jack looked up the stairs. The green light was there. Small. Far. Always far.

"Wait," he said. "Wait for me."

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
Poppy the rabbit hopped down the path. Sam ran to catch her. Then Sam fell.

"Oh no," Sam said. "My knee hurts."

Sam sat on the grass. The scrape was red and sore. Mom came out the door and sat too.

"I can carry you inside," Mom said.

"No," said Sam. "I want to stay with Poppy."

Mom put a bandage on the knee. It had tiny stars on it. Sam felt better.

Later, Sam and Poppy went for a walk. They came to the bridge over the river. It was late at night. The moon was up.

Sam looked at the water. Far away, on the bridge, a small green light shone. It was just one little light. Sam wanted to touch it.

"Can we go there?" Sam asked.

"No," said Mom. "It is too far."

Sam looked at the green light. It was so pretty. Then Sam looked at Poppy and the stars on the knee. That was enough for now.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
Poppy the rabbit hopped too fast and fell down. She scraped her knee on a rock. It hurt a lot.

Sam heard her cry. He ran out the door. He picked Poppy up. He did not carry her far. He sat her on a soft log.

"Ouch," said Poppy. "My knee is sore."

"I will help you," said Sam. He put a leaf on it. The leaf was tiny and cool.

Poppy felt better. Sam felt glad. They went for a slow walk. They came to a bridge over the river. It was late at night.

Sam saw a green light. It shone far away across the water. It was small and bright.

"What is that?" said Poppy.

"I do not know," said Sam. "But I want it."

He looked and looked. The light did not come closer. It just blinked and stayed.

"Come on," said Poppy. "My knee feels good now."

Sam looked back one more time. Then he walked home with Poppy. The green light stayed far away.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
Poppy the rabbit ran fast and fell down. She scraped her knee on a rock. It hurt. Sam heard her cry and ran to help.

"Poor Poppy," Sam said. "Your knee is red."

Sam put a soft cloth on it. He wanted to carry her home. The night was dark and late.

They went down the path to the bridge over the river. On the bridge, Sam saw a tiny light. It was green and small and far away. It shone on the water.

"What is that?" Sam asked.

"I don't know," said Poppy.

Sam wanted to touch the green light. He reached out his hand. The light stayed far away. He took a step. Then another.

"Sam," said Poppy. "My knee."

Sam turned back. He helped Poppy hop along. At home, he opened the door. But he thought of the green light on the bridge. He thought of it all night. He wanted it so much. He wanted it, and he could not have it.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
Poppy the rabbit skipped down the garden path and tripped on a stone. Sam ran to her. "Oh no, your knee!"

Poppy looked at her knee. It was red and scraped. "It hurts," she said.

Sam picked her up. "I will carry you home," he said. He opened the door and set her on a soft chair.

Then Sam saw it. Far away, a small light shone on the bridge over the river. It was green and quiet.

"Stay here," Sam said. He walked to the bridge. The light was still there.

"Come back," Poppy called. "My knee hurts!"

But Sam stared at the light. He reached for it. The light stayed far away.

"Come back to Poppy," she said.

Sam looked at the bridge. He looked at the tiny light. He wanted it. He wanted it so much.

"Come back," Poppy said again.

Sam did not move. The light was small and green. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it.

Poppy cried. Sam ran back and held her. But all night he thought of the light.

stories.topic: a rabbit and a scraped knee
stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
Please open the door, Sam said. Sam was a small rabbit.

Sam had a scraped knee. He fell on a rock.

Ouch, said Sam. My knee hurts.

His mom put a bandage on it. She said, I will carry you home.

But Sam did not want to go home. He wanted to see the light.

The light is on the bridge, Sam said. The light is on the bridge.

Mom said, It is late at night. We must go.

The light is on the bridge, Sam said again. I want the light.

His mom picked him up. She carried him past the door.

Sam looked at the bridge. A tiny green light shone on the bridge over the river.

I want it, said Sam. I want the light.

You cannot have it, said Mom. It is far away.

The light is on the bridge, Sam said. The light is on the bridge.

His knee hurt. But he only looked at the light.

The light is on the bridge, he said. I want the light.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
One big bear named Tom lived in a cave with a leaky roof. Drip, drip, drip went the water on his nose.

Tom put a tin pot under the hole. He put a big leaf on top. Nothing worked.

Late at night, Tom went for a walk. He came to a bridge over the river. Far away, a little light shone on the water. It was small and green. It made Tom feel shy and warm inside. He wanted to touch it. He did not know how.

Tom found a round button in his pocket. He set it on the bridge rail. "Stay," he said. Then he went home.

In the morning, Tom climbed up high. He pushed moss into the roof hole. He sang a song and did a hop. The leak stopped!

That night, Tom sat in his dry cave. He thought of the little light. It was far, but it was there. He smiled and slept.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
One big bear named Tom lived in a little house. Rain came in through a hole in the roof. Drip, drip, drip. Tom put a pot under the hole. He put a pan there too. The floor got wet.

Late at night, Tom went out to find help. He walked to the bridge over the river. Far away, he saw a soft light. It was small and green. It did not move. It did not come closer. Tom felt shy. He wanted to touch it. He could not.

He saw a button on the bridge. He did not pick it up. He looked at the light again. It was still far away. His house was still wet.

Tom gave a hop. Then he went home. He climbed on the roof. He put a leaf over the hole. He put mud on the leaf. The rain stopped coming in.

Tom sat by the fire. He was warm. He was dry. He did not need the far light. His own small lamp was near. It was enough. The end.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
One night a bear named Tom heard a drip. The roof of his little house had a leak. He put a pot under it. Drip, drip, drip.

Tom could not sleep. He went for a walk. The moon was up. The town was quiet.

On the bridge over the river, Tom saw a small light. It was far away and low. It was green and soft. It did not move. Tom wanted to touch it. He took a hop. He took two. The light stayed far away. Tom felt shy. He put his paw on the rail.

He walked home. Drip, drip, drip. He saw the light again in his mind. He looked out the window. There it was, small and green.

Tom found a button in his pocket. He sewed it on his old hat. He climbed the roof. He pushed the button into the hole. The drip stopped.

The green light still shone far away. Tom did not need to reach it. He had his warm house. He had his quiet night. He smiled and slept.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
Outside the rain came down. Tom the bear put a pot under the drip. The roof leaked. Drip, drip. Tom fixed it with a button and some tape. It still leaked.

Late at night Tom went for a walk. He came to a bridge over the river. Far away, a small light shone. It was soft and green. It sat on the water and would not come close. Tom wanted to hold it. He took a hop. Then a step. The light stayed far.

He went home. The pot was full. He fixed the roof with mud and leaves. It still leaked.

Back on the bridge, the light was there. Tom felt shy. He said, "Come here." The light did not come. He reached. He reached.

One night Tom brought the button. He set it on the rail. The light touched it, just a little. Then the rain stopped. The roof held. Tom smiled. The light stayed far, but Tom slept warm and dry.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Tom

axes.where: on a bridge over the river

stories.text:
One night Tom the bear heard a drip. The roof had a leak. He put a pot under it. The pot went plink, plink.

Then Tom saw a light. It was far away, on a bridge over the river. The light was small and green. It made his chest feel warm. He wanted it. He wanted it so much.

He left the pot. He walked to the river. The light sat on the bridge, low and soft. It did not come closer. It did not go away.

Tom put one paw out. The light stayed far. He was shy. He did not hop. He just looked.

He looked all night. The light was still there. His fur got cold. His eyes got tired.

Then he heard a sound. His button fell off his coat. It rolled on the bridge. Tom bent down to get it. When he stood up, the sun was up. The green light was gone.

Tom walked home. The pot was full. The roof still dripped. But Tom felt happy. He had seen the light. That was enough for now.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
The rain came in through the roof. Omar the bear put a pot under the drip. Plink, plink, plink. He did not like that sound.

His friend Tilly the turtle came by. "We can fix it," she said. So they climbed up. Omar held a big leaf. Tilly held a soft cloth. They pushed and patched. Still it dripped.

They went to the pond for mud to plug the hole. The sun was warm. The water was clear. Deep down, Omar saw a small light. It glowed green, like a tiny feather floating. He wanted it. He reached down. He could not touch it. The pond was too deep.

"Come on," said Tilly. She helped him lift a heavy stone of mud.

They climbed back and fixed the roof. No more drip. Then Omar looked at the pond again. The green light was still there, far down, waiting.

Tilly smiled. "That is just the sun on a bottle," she said. Omar looked once more. He still wanted it. But he had a dry roof, and that was enough for today.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
The bear named Omar lived in a warm cave. But after many sunny afternoons, drip, drip, drip came from his roof. A leaky roof is a sad thing for a bear. Omar put a soft leaf under the drip. The leaf got full. He put a feather there too. The feather got wet and flat.

“I can fix it,” said his friend Tilly. She came with a big pot. They put the pot under the drip. Drip, drip, drip. The pot got full too.

Omar looked out at the pond. Deep at the bottom, a small green light was shining. It was always there. He wanted to touch it. He reached down, but the water only gave him cold paws. “Come back,” said Tilly.

So Omar came back. He and Tilly used mud and sticks. They patched the roof. No more drip. Then Omar saw the light again in the pond. It was pretty. But he did not lift a paw. “Some lights stay where they are,” said Tilly. Omar nodded. The roof was dry. That was enough.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
The rain came in. Omar the bear put a pot under the drip. Drip, drip, drip. The roof of his den had a hole.

Omar climbed up to look. He saw a pond far away. Deep down in the pond, something glowed. A small green light. It was tiny and far.

Omar wanted it. He climbed down. He walked to the pond. He stood at the edge. The light was so deep. He could not reach it.

His friend Pip the rabbit came. "What do you see?" she asked.

"A light," said Omar. "It is soft and green. I want it."

Pip gave him a feather. "This will not lift the light," she said. "But it can tick a nose."

Omar laughed. He looked at the pond again. The light was still there. Still far. He wanted it.

Then Pip said, "Your roof is leaking."

Omar blinked. Oh yes. The roof. The rain. The pot.

They went home. Pip held the feather. Omar found soft moss. They filled the hole. The drip stopped.

Omar looked back once at the pond. The light was gone. But his den was dry.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
The rain came in through the roof again. Omar the bear put a pot under the drip. Then he put a cup. Then he put his best red boot.

His friend Tilly the goose came over. "I can help," she said. She brought a big leaf and a feather. She held the leaf over the hole. The drip slowed to a soft tap.

Omar was glad. But then he saw it. Deep at the bottom of the pond, past the tall grass, something glowed. A small green light. It shimmered in the sunny afternoon.

"Stay with the roof," said Tilly.

Omar did not stay. He waded in. The light was so far down. He reached. He could not lift it. He reached again. "I want it. I want it. I want it."

Tilly pulled him back by his fur. "The roof, Omar."

He blinked. The drip had stopped. The twist? The green light was only a frog's eye, blinking slow. Omar laughed and went home to his pot, his cup, and his boot.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Omar

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
The roof leaked. Omar the bear put a pot under the drip. Plip, plop. The pot filled up.

Omar went outside for a walk. The sun was warm. He saw a pond.

Deep down in the pond, a small green light glowed. Omar stared at it. He wanted it. He wanted it so much.

He reached into the water. The light was too deep. He reached again. The light slid away.

"Come here, light," Omar said. "Come here. Come here. Come here."

His friend Rosa the duck came by. "What do you see?" she asked.

"That light," Omar said. "I want it. I want it. I want it."

Rosa gave him a feather. "It is soft," she said. "Use it to lift the light."

Omar tried. The feather tickled the water. The light laughed and sank deeper.

Omar sat down. He felt sad. Then he saw something. The light was not a light. It was a shiny fish.

Omar went home. The pot was full. He fixed the roof with a soft cloth. No more drip. But at night, he still dreamed of the little green light at the bottom of the pond.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
Please fix the hole, said Ella. The rain comes in. The bear looked up. He was big and brown. He did not want to climb.

Ella put a feather on the hole. The feather did not stay. She made a wiggle with her nose. She put a clean cloth on the hole. The cloth got wet.

The sun was warm. On top of a far hill, a small light shone. It was yellow and soft. Ella saw it once. It looked like a dry, warm place. Then she turned back to the roof.

The bear would not help. So Ella climbed up alone. She was small. The roof was high. She fell down. The bear did not catch her.

That night, the rain came in. It fell on Ella. It fell on the bear. The light on the hill stayed far away. No one went to get it.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text: Puddles grew on the floor of Ella’s cave. The roof had a leak. Drip, drip, drip. Ella was a bear who liked things neat. She got a bucket. She got a mop. She made the cave clean. But the drip came back. She put a big leaf over the hole. The leaf went wiggle, wiggle, then fell down. She put a soft feather in the crack. The water pushed it out. Drip, drip, drip. Ella sat down. Her fur got wet. Then she looked out. On top of a far hill, a small light shone in the sunny afternoon. It was not the sun. It was a tiny, warm gleam. Ella wanted to touch it. She wanted to hold it. But the hill was too far. She turned back to the bucket. Drip, drip, drip. She tried a flat rock. The water went around it. She tried mud. The water went through it. The light on the far hill stayed bright. Ella could not reach it. She could not fix the roof. She lay down in the wet. Drip, drip, drip.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Ella

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
Pitter patter went the rain on Ella’s roof. The bear cub sat in her cozy cave and frowned. A drop fell on her nose. Then another. Her roof had a little leak.

Ella found a soft feather. She pushed it into the crack. It did not work. She gave a wiggle to a big leaf. She pressed it on top. The water still came through. She tried to clean the wet floor with moss. More drips fell.

Ella went outside for a walk. The sun was warm. On top of a far hill, she saw a small shine. It was bright and still. It looked like a place where nothing was wet. It looked like a dry, happy home.
