But behind the hedge, the light was waiting. It was small and far. It blinked.

Hugo left the piano. He walked to the window. The light was still there. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it. He could not reach it. He never could.

He went back to the piano. He patted the keys. But the song was gone.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Summer was hot, and Tom found a piano. It sat in the cool room like a big brown stone. Tom was a small kitten. He put one paw on a key. Ping! The sound was soft and round.

Tom wanted to play a song. He tried and tried. His paws went clack, clack, plop. No song came out. A drop of sweat ran down his nose.

His friend Ben came in. Ben was a big cat. "I can help," said Ben. Ben put Tom on the bench. Ben pressed the keys. Tom pressed too. Ping, ping, plop!

At the top of the stairs, a small light glowed. It was green and far away. Tom looked up. He reached one paw toward it. The light did not come closer. Tom blinked, then turned back to the piano.

Ben and Tom played again. Ding, dong, ping! A happy song filled the room. Tom's ears went rosy. He did not need the far light. He had a friend and a song.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Summer was hot and Tom was a small gray kitten. He sat on the cool stone floor by the piano. His paws went tap tap on the keys. The piano made a loud sound. Tom jumped back.

Then he saw it. At the top of the stairs, a small green light was glowing. It was like a little star. Tom wanted it. He put one paw on the first step.

His friend Ben the bird flew down. "What do you see?" Ben asked.

"A green light," Tom said. "I want it."

Ben looked up the stairs. "I see it too," he said. "I can help you."

Tom climbed up and up. The stairs were warm. A drop of water fell from his nose. His ears were rosy and hot. The light was still far away. It always stayed far away.

Ben flew beside him. "Let's rest here," Ben said. So they rested.

Tom did not reach the light. But Ben sang a song for him. Tom purred. The light twinkled like a happy hello. Tom was happy with his friend.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text: Summer was hot, and Tom the kitten found a piano. It was big and brown. Tom put one paw on a key. Plink! He liked the sound. He sat on the cool stone floor and played. Plink, plink, plunk. His friend Ben the bird came to help. Ben sang along. The song was small and happy. Then Tom saw it. At the top of the stairs, a green light glowed. It was soft and far. Tom wanted it. He climbed one step. Then two. But the light did not come close. He felt a drop of sweat on his nose. Ben flew to him. "Come back and play," Ben said. So Tom went back to the piano. He played a rosy, happy song. The green light stayed up high. It was pretty. But Tom did not need it. He had a song, and he had a friend. The sun went down, and Tom was happy. Plink, plink, plunk.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Sometimes Tom the kitten sat on the piano bench. The keys were warm. It was a hot summer day.

Tom put one paw on a key. Plink. He put another paw down. Plonk. He wanted to play a real song.

Then he saw it. At the top of the stairs, a small green light. It glowed on the wall like a tiny sun.

Tom forgot the piano. He climbed the stairs. The steps were hard like stone. The light stayed far away.

"Come back," said his friend Ben the bird. "Play with me."

Tom did not hear. He reached for the light. He could not touch it.

His small heart gave a drop. He felt sad and lonely.

Ben flew to him. Ben sang a soft, rosy song. Tom's ears went up.

"Sing with me," said Ben.

Tom went back down. He put his paws on the keys. Plink, plonk, plink. Ben sang. Tom played. The green light blinked above, but Tom was happy now.

stories.name: Tom

axes.where: at the top of the stairs

stories.text:
Summer was hot, and Tom the kitten found a piano. He put one paw on a key. Plink. He put another paw on a key. Plonk. The piano was warm and big.

Then Tom saw the light. It was at the top of the stairs. It was small and green.

Tom wanted the light. He left the piano.

He climbed one step. The step was like a stone.

"Come back," said his friend Ben.

Tom did not come back. He looked up at the light. The light did not drop down. It did not come close.

"Come back," said Ben.

Tom reached. He reached and reached. The light stayed high.

"Come back," said Ben.

Tom's nose was rosy. His paws were tired. He sat down on the step.

Ben came up. Ben sat with him. "The light is far," said Ben. "But I am here."

Tom looked at Ben. Then Tom heard the piano. Plink. Plonk.

Tom went down the stairs. He put his paw on a key. Ben put his paw on a key. They made a happy song. Tom did not need the light. He had a friend.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: in a window across the street

stories.text:
Sometimes a fire truck and a kitten can be friends. Lena knew this was true. She had a little kitten named Puff. Puff was soft and small.

One day a fire truck came to her street. It was big and red. The fire fighters let Lena sit inside. Puff sat on her lap. Puff did not like the loud noise. Puff sneezed. It was very funny. Lena laughed and laughed.

Soon it was just before bedtime. The moon came up. Lena put on her cozy pajamas. She went to her window.

Across the street, a small light glowed in a window. It was green. It looked like a tiny fire truck light. Lena wanted to touch it. She reached out her hand. She could not reach. The light stayed far away.

She had to pull her hand back inside. Puff curled up on her bed. Lena yawned. The green light was still there. She closed her eyes.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: in a window across the street

stories.text:
Soft pajamas on, Lena heard a fire truck go by. It made a loud, happy siren. She ran to the window to see it.

A tiny kitten sat on the truck. The kitten looked silly in a fire hat. Lena laughed so hard she almost fell over. That was the funny part.

Then Lena saw a small green light in a window across the street. It blinked once. She thought about the kitten and smiled.

Her mom said it was time for bed. The moon was up. Lena had to pull her cozy blanket to her chin. The green light blinked again. Lena waved at it.

She wanted to go to that window. She wanted to hold that little light. But her eyes felt heavy.

The green light stayed far away. It always stayed far away. Lena closed her eyes. She dreamed of a kitten on a fire truck, and a light she could not reach.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: in a window across the street

stories.text:
Sirens meant the fire truck was coming. Lena heard it first. She ran to the window.

A tiny kitten rode on the truck's bumper. It looked wet and scared. The truck stopped. A firefighter lifted the kitten down.

Lena laughed. The kitten sneezed on the firefighter's nose. That was funny.

Then Lena saw the light. Across the street, a small light glowed in a window. It was green and soft. It looked like the moon stayed up late.

She put her hands on the glass. She wanted to pull it close. She wanted to hold it. But it was far away.

"Bedtime," said Mom.

Lena climbed into her cozy bed. She thought of the kitten. She thought of the light. The light pulled at her, gentle and far.

She reached one hand out. Her fingers touched only air. The light stayed across the street. She could not reach it. She never could.

She closed her eyes. The green light glowed behind them.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: in a window across the street

stories.text:
Sometimes a fire truck comes down our street. Lena loves the big red truck. It is loud and brave.

One night, just before bed, a small kitten sat in the road. A fire truck had to stop.

Lena laughed. The kitten did not move. It just washed its face. That was funny.

Then Lena saw a light. It was in a window across the street.

The light was green. It was small and far. It did not move.

Lena wanted that light. She did not know why. She felt a pull in her chest.

The moon came up. Her room felt cozy. But Lena went to the window.

She reached out her hand. She could not touch the light. It stayed across the street.

She looked at the light again. And again. And again.

Her mom said, “Come to bed, Lena.”

Lena whispered, “I want the light.”

She climbed into bed. She left the light on. It was small and green in her mind. She reached for it in her dreams.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: in a window across the street

stories.text:
Sometimes a fire truck comes down our street. Lena likes the loud bell. One night a kitten sat on the truck. It was funny. The kitten did not move. Lena laughed.

Then she saw the light. A small green light. It was in a window across the street.

Lena went to her window. The moon was up. She wanted to pull the light close. She reached out. She could not touch it.

The light stayed there. Lena reached again. She reached and reached.

Come here, light. Come here, light.

Her bed was cozy. But she did not get in. She watched the light. The light did not come.

Come here, light. Come here, light.

The kitten was warm and small. But Lena watched the light. She reached. She could not have it.

Come here, light. Come here, light.

Her eyes got heavy. The light stayed far away. Lena kept reaching.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Milo the fire truck slept at the station. Kai liked to sit in it. One cold autumn evening, a tiny kitten climbed in. It was stuck behind the big red wheel. Kai heard a soft mew. He had a little problem.

Kai pulled his wagon to the station. He did not grab the kitten. He was quiet. He gave it warm milk. The kitten walked out slow. Kai smiled.

Then Kai saw a small light on top of a far hill. It blinked once. It looked like a warm window. He wanted to go there. But the kitten was safe now. That was good. The light blinked again. Kai held the kitten close. He thought, someday I will walk to that hill. Not tonight. Tonight the kitten needs me. The light stayed far away. Kai did not mind.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Mittens sat on Kai's red wagon. Kai pulled the wagon down the street. The air was cold. It was a late autumn evening. Kai heard a small mew. A kitten was stuck under a bush.

Kai tried to grab the kitten. The kitten was too scared. It ran away. Kai felt sad. Then Kai heard a loud sound. A fire truck came down the street. It stopped near the bush. The fire fighter smiled. She had a quiet voice. She showed Kai how to hold a soft blanket. The kitten liked the blanket. Kai picked up the kitten.

Kai put the kitten in the wagon. The fire truck drove away. Kai looked up at the far hill. A tiny light shone there. It was warm and yellow. Kai wanted to touch it. But the light stayed far away. Kai held the kitten close. The kitten was warm. That was good. Kai pulled the wagon home.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Maybe the fire truck came today. Kai heard the big engine rumble down the street. He ran outside with his red wagon. A tiny kitten sat on the curb. It shook in the cold autumn evening.

Kai tried to grab the kitten. The kitten ran under a bush. It was too scared. Kai had a little problem. How do you help a scared kitten?

He put his wagon near the bush. He sat very quiet. The kitten peeked out. Then it climbed into the warm wagon. Kai pulled it home.

On top of a far hill, a small light glowed. It was soft and yellow. It looked like a place where lost things go. Kai saw it every night. He wished he could roll his wagon up there. He wished the light would come down to him. He looked at the kitten. The kitten looked back.

The light stayed far away. But the kitten was close. Kai held it tight. The light blinked once. Maybe someday he would reach it. Not tonight. Tonight he had a warm little friend.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: Maybe the fire truck can help. Kai pulled his red wagon down the street. A tiny kitten sat by the fence. It was stuck and afraid. The fire truck came with a loud siren. Kai did not grab the kitten. He was too small. The firefighters were busy. So Kai made a plan. He put a soft blanket in his wagon. He rolled it close. The kitten sniffed. Then it hopped in. Kai felt happy. But then he looked up. Far away, on top of the hill, a little light blinked. It was warm and small. It called to him. He wanted to touch it. He wanted to hold it. The kitten mewed. The sky turned gray. The cold wind blew. Kai should go home. But that light stayed on the hill. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it. The firefighters waved good-bye. Kai held the kitten. Still he looked at the hill. The light blinked and blinked. He whispered, I want to go there. But his wagon was heavy. The quiet street waited. So Kai walked home. The light stayed far away.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Kai

axes.where: on top of a far hill
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Maybe the fire truck can help the kitten. Kai pulled his red wagon down the street. A small kitten sat in the wagon. It was cold. The kitten shivered.

"Hold on," Kai said. He wrapped the kitten in his scarf.

The fire truck came. It was big and loud. But the kitten was safe now. Kai held it close.

Then Kai saw it. On top of the far hill, a little light glowed. It was green. It was soft. It was so far away.

"Oh," Kai said. "Oh, oh, oh."

He wanted to touch it. He wanted to hold it. He wanted it more than anything.

"Kai," said his mom. "Let's grab some dinner."

But Kai just looked at the light. "Oh, oh, oh."

The kitten meowed. It was hungry. Kai blinked. He picked up the kitten. He pulled the wagon home.

It was quiet. The light stayed far away. But the kitten was warm. That was enough. For now.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
By the station, Rosa heard a tiny mew. A kitten sat on the big red fire truck. It was early morning. The sky was gloomy and gray.

Rosa picked up the kitten. She gave it a warm bath. The kitten did a funny shake. Water flew everywhere. Rosa laughed.

She lit a candle for light. Then she saw something far away. A small green light shone on a boat out on the lake. It blinked once. Then twice. Rosa wanted to touch it. She reached her hand out. The light stayed far away.

The kitten climbed her arm. It purred. Rosa smiled and held it close. The green light was still there. But her arms were full.

She fed the kitten and named it Sparky. They sat by the window. The light faded with the morning. Rosa did not need to reach anymore.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Big red fire truck came down Rosa's street. A tiny kitten sat high in a tree. It could not come down.

Rosa waved at the fire fighters. One climbed up with a soft net. The kitten said meow. Then it sneezed. Everyone laughed. That was funny.

The sky was gloomy. Rosa held a candle in her window. It made a small warm glow.

Then she saw it. On a boat out on the lake, a green light shone. It was early morning. The boat rocked. The light did not shake. It just stayed there, far away.

Rosa reached out her hand. She wanted that light. She could not have it.

The kitten purred in her arms. Rosa looked at the tree. Then she looked back at the lake.

The green light was still there. Small. Far. Waiting. Rosa watched it until breakfast.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Bella the kitten sat on the fire truck. Rosa was a firefighter. She drove the big red truck.

One early morning, Rosa drove to the lake. A boat was stuck. The sky was gloomy. Rosa felt sad.

Then Rosa saw a small light. It was green. It sat on the boat out on the lake. Rosa wanted to touch it. She reached out her hand. The light was too far.

Bella jumped on the boat. She slipped on a fish. Splash! Bella got wet. Rosa laughed. It was funny.

Rosa lit a candle. The little flame danced. She wanted the green light. She reached again. It still was far.

Bella began to shake. Rosa held her close. The boat rocked. The green light blinked. Rosa could not have it.

She sailed home with Bella. The light stayed on the water. Rosa looked back. She wished and wished.

Bella purred. Rosa smiled. The light was still there. It was always there.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
By the station, Rosa heard a tiny mew. A kitten sat by the big fire truck. Rosa gave it warm milk from a blue bowl.

Then she saw the light. A small green glow, far out on the lake. It sat on a boat, still and steady.

Rosa ran to the shore. "Come back!" she called. The kitten ran too. It tripped on a rope and rolled like a fuzzy ball. Rosa laughed so hard she had to shake her head. That was the funny part.

But the green light stayed on the boat. It did not come closer.

The morning felt gloomy. Rosa lit a candle on the dock. Its flame was small and orange. The green light was small and green. Her light could not reach it.

She wanted that boat. She wanted that light. She reached out her hand.

The kitten climbed her leg and sat on her shoulder. It purred.

Rosa looked at the green light again. It blinked once, twice.

She held the kitten close. The boat drifted away. The light stayed far. She could not have it. She reached anyway.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
By the station, Rosa heard a tiny mew. A kitten sat on the fire truck. Rosa gave it warm milk.

Then she saw the light. A small green light, far out on the lake. It sat on a boat. The boat rocked in the early morning.

Rosa reached for the light. Her fingers found only cold air.

The kitten climbed her leg. It sneezed. Milk went on her nose. Rosa laughed. That was funny.

But the light blinked. Rosa stopped laughing. She reached again. The boat did not come.

A candle burned low on the sill. Its flame made her shadow shake. The sky looked gloomy and gray.

Rosa held the kitten. She whispered to the light. Come here. Come here. Come here.

The kitten purred. The light stayed far away. Rosa reached. The light stayed. She reached. The light stayed.

Come here. Come here. Come here.

The morning grew bright. The light grew small. Rosa still reached.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Ravi

axes.where: across a big field

stories.text:
A fire truck came down Ravi's street. It was red and shiny. Ravi waved at the driver. The driver waved back.

Then Ravi heard a small sound. A kitten sat on a wall. It was stuck. The kitten was scared.

"Hold on!" said Ravi. He ran to get help. The fire truck stopped. A firefighter picked up the kitten. She gave it a warm hug. The kitten licked her nose.

Ravi laughed. It was funny. The kitten tried to eat his cake. He had to push it away. The firefighter was jolly. Everyone clapped.

Later, the sky turned orange. Ravi sat on the grass. Far away, across a big field, a small green light blinked. It was a tiny lamp on a porch. Pretty, he thought. He wished he could touch it. But the field was wide. The light stayed far.

The kitten curled up on his lap. Ravi smiled. The green light blinked again. He watched it until the stars came out.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Ravi

axes.where: across a big field

stories.text:
A fire truck came down Ravi's street. It was big and red. It went wee-ooo, wee-ooo. Ravi ran to see it.

A tiny kitten sat on the truck. The kitten was scared. Ravi wanted to help.

"Stop!" Ravi said. The truck stopped.

Ravi gave the kitten some cake. The kitten ate it. It licked its paw. Ravi laughed. The kitten had cake on its nose!

Ravi felt jolly. He said, "I will push you home in my wagon."

Then Ravi saw a small light. It was far away, across a big field. The light was green. It blinked in the sunset.

Ravi looked at the light. He wanted to touch it.

"Come on," he said to the kitten. They went to the field. The light was still far.

Ravi walked and walked. The light did not get closer. The sun went down.

Ravi felt sad. He could not reach the green light.

He held the kitten close. The light blinked once more. Then it was gone. Ravi went home with the kitten. That was good.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Ravi

axes.where: across a big field

stories.text: A fire truck came down Ravi's street. It was big and red. It went wee-ooo, wee-ooo. Ravi ran to see it. A tiny kitten sat on the truck. The kitten was scared. Ravi said, "Do not be scared, little cat." The fire truck stopped. The firemen got out. They were jolly. One fireman gave Ravi a piece of cake. The kitten tried to eat the cake. It got cake on its nose. Ravi laughed. That was funny. Then Ravi saw a small green light. It was across a big field. The light blinked once. It blinked again. Ravi wanted to push through the field to it. He took one step. The kitten mewed. Ravi stopped. He gave the kitten a soft push back onto the truck. The green light was still there. It was far away. Ravi looked at it. He looked at the kitten. The light did not come closer. It never did. The sun went down. The green light stayed across the field, small and far, and Ravi could not have it.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Ravi

axes.where: across a big field

stories.text:
A fire truck came down the street. Ravi heard the loud siren. He ran to the window to see it.

The fire truck was red and big. It stopped near the park. A kitten sat in a tree and could not get down. The fire truck came to help the kitten.

Ravi clapped his hands. "Good fire truck!" he said.

Far away, across the big field, a small light blinked. It was green and soft. The sun was going down at sunset. The light glowed on and on.

Ravi looked at the kitten. Then he looked at the light.

The kitten was safe now. A fireman held it and gave it a little cake. The kitten ate the cake. It was funny. The kitten got cake on its nose.

Ravi wanted to push the door open. He wanted to run to the light. He wanted to hold it.

He said, "I want the light. I want the light. I want the light." He said it again and again. The jolly firemen did not hear him. The kitten did not hear him. Only Ravi saw the green light across the big field, and he could not reach it.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Ravi

axes.where: across a big field

stories.text:
A fire truck came down Ravi's street. It was red and loud. Ravi clapped his hands.

A tiny kitten sat on the truck. The kitten was small and soft.

"Beep beep!" said the truck.

"Meow!" said the kitten.

Ravi laughed. That was funny.

Then Ravi saw the light. It was green. It was far away. It was across the big field.

"Oh," said Ravi. "The green light."

The sun went down. The sky turned pink and gold.

Ravi looked at the green light. He wanted it. He wanted it so much.

"Come here, light," said Ravi. "Come here."

The kitten climbed on Ravi's cake. The cake was for his birthday.

"Silly kitten," said Ravi. But he did not smile.

He gave the kitten a little push. "Go get the light," he said.

The kitten just purred.

Ravi watched the light. The light did not come.

"Come here," he said. "Come here. Come here."

His mother called him in. The jolly truck drove away.

Ravi stayed. He looked across the big field.

"Come here," he said. "Come here. Come here."

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a pole by the gate

stories.text:
Hurry, Nate heard the fire truck come down the street. A small kitten sat in the road and would not move. Nate ran to help. The truck went slow. It did not hit the kitten. Nate wrapped the kitten in a blanket.

His friend Anna helped him look for the kitten's home. They went to every gate. The kitten just wanted to chase leaves.

The sun went down. On a pole by the gate, a small green light came on. It blinked and blinked. Nate wished he could hold it in his hand. He could not reach it. He did not try long.

Then a lady said, "That is my kitten!" Nate gave the kitten back. The lady smiled big.

A friend helps when you need it, and a helper's heart feels warm.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a pole by the gate

stories.text:
Here is Nate. Nate has a fire truck. It is red and big. Nate loves to push it fast.

One day, Nate sees a small kitten. The kitten is cold. It sits by the gate. Nate wants to help. He gets his soft blanket. He wraps the kitten up.

A friend comes by. Her name is May. May says, "We must be slow and kind."

Nate and May play with the kitten. The kitten likes to chase a little ball. The fire truck can wait.

The sun goes down. The sky is orange and pink. Nate looks up. On a pole by the gate, a light comes on. It is a small, far light. It is a soft, green glow. Nate can see it but he cannot touch it. He feels a pull. He looks and looks. Then he pats the kitten. The kitten is warm now.

A friend helps you. And a small warm thing is good to hold.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a pole by the gate

stories.text:
Henry the fire truck slept at the station. Nate loved Henry. Nate was four. One day a kitten came to the station. The kitten was small and soft. Nate named her Mittens.

Mittens was scared. She hid under a blanket. Nate said, "Come out, Mittens." Mittens did not come out. Nate and his friend Sam sat down. They were very slow and quiet. Mittens came out. She licked Nate's hand.

Then Mittens ran to the gate. Nate and Sam had to chase her. The sun went down. The sky was pink and red. On a pole by the gate, a little light came on. It was green. It blinked and blinked. Nate stopped. He looked at the green light. He wanted to touch it. He could not. It was too high.

Sam said, "Nate, come. We have Mittens." Nate looked at the light one more time. Then he carried Mittens back inside. The green light stayed on the pole. Nate could not reach it. But he had his friend and his kitten. That was enough for tonight. A friend helps you when you want something you cannot have.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a pole by the gate

stories.text:
Hurry, Nate said. The fire truck is here. It is big and red. A kitten sits on the step. The kitten is small and scared. Nate wants to help. He gets his soft blanket.

The sun goes down. On a pole by the gate, a little green light turns on. It shines and shines. Nate looks at it. He wants to touch it. He cannot reach it. The light is far away.

His friend May comes. She says, Nate, look at the kitten. The kitten shakes. Nate puts the blanket on the kitten. The kitten is warm now.

Nate looks back at the light. It blinks at him. He wants it. He wants it. He says, I want it. May says, Come on. Let us chase the kitten.

They run slow so the kitten can follow. The kitten is happy. Nate is happy too. The green light is still on the pole. But the kitten is here. That is better.

A friend helps you see what is right in front of you.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a pole by the gate

stories.text:
Here comes the fire truck! Nate runs to the gate. A little kitten is stuck on the truck. Nate wants to help. The sun goes down.

The sky is orange. On a pole by the gate, a small light turns on. It is green. It glows. Nate sees it.

He wants to hold that light. He wants it so much.

"Nate," says his friend May. "Hold the blanket."

Nate does not hear. He looks at the green light. He wants it. He wants it. He wants it.

"Chase the kitten," says May. "Slow and soft."

Nate says, "I want the light. I want the light."

May pulls him. "The kitten needs you."

Nate blinks. He wraps the kitten in the blanket. He holds it close. The green light shines, far away. He cannot have it. But the kitten is warm in his arms.

You cannot hold every pretty thing, but you can hold what needs you.

stories.name: Ella

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
The squirrel's stash was small but safe. Ella had counted every nut. She kept them under the old oak tree.

Late at night, she woke up hungry. She ran to the tree. A soft feather lay on the snow. Her stash was gone! A big wind had blown the leaves away.

Ella did a little chase around the trunk. She found one dusty nut near a root. Then she saw a light across the snowy yard. It was green and far away. It made her stop. She wanted to touch it. She took one step. The light did not move.

Ella shook her tail. She went back to the tree. She dug under the roots. There were all her nuts, warm and dry. The light stayed across the yard, pretty and far. Ella did not need it. She had her stash. She ate a nut and went home happy.

stories.name: Ella

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
The squirrel hid nuts under the old oak tree. Ella watched him from her window. He was busy. He was quick. He had a little stash for winter.

Ella wanted to help. But she did not want to scare him. She put on her boots. The snow was deep. It was late at night.

Across the snowy yard, a small green light glowed. It was far away. Ella looked at it. She felt a pull. She wanted to go to it. But she stayed with the squirrel.

The squirrel dropped a nut. It rolled away. A problem! Ella picked it up. She gave it back. The squirrel took it. He ran off.

Ella found a feather in the snow. It was dusty and light. She did not chase the green light. She went home.

The next morning, the squirrel came back. He left a nut on her step. Ella smiled. She had a friend now. The green light was still far away. But she was happy.

stories.name: Ella

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
The squirrel hid nuts for winter. Ella watched from her window. She counted each one. Her little problem was simple. She could not sleep. She wanted those nuts for her own soup.

Late at night, she saw a light. It was small and green. It glowed across the snowy yard. It sat under the big oak tree. That is where the squirrel kept its stash.

Ella put on her boots. She went outside. The snow was dusty and deep. She tried to chase the light. It moved away. She reached for it. It was always far.

She found a feather in the snow. She held it tight. The light blinked once. Then it went out.

Ella felt sad. Then she heard a tiny sound. The squirrel came back. It dropped one nut at her feet. Ella smiled. She gave the squirrel her feather. They shared the stash. Ella went home warm and happy.

stories.name: Ella

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: The squirrel's stash was small but safe. Ella counted nuts under the old oak. Three for winter. Two for a snack. Then she saw it across the snowy yard. A green light. It glowed near the fence. Ella forgot her nuts. She ran to the light. She left the stash open. A dusty wind blew snow on the nuts. A feather flew by. Ella did not chase it. She chased the light. The light stayed far away. It always stayed far away. Her stash got cold. Her stash got lost. Ella felt sad. Then she heard a little chirp. Her friend Pip came. Pip helped her find the nuts. They put them back in the oak. The light blinked once. Ella did not run. She stayed with Pip. They shared one nut. Her stash was small but safe again.

stories.name: Ella

axes.where: across the snowy yard
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
The squirrel hid nuts under the old oak tree. Ella watched from her window. She counted each nut. She wanted that stash.

Then she saw it. Across the snowy yard, a small green light glowed. It twinkled like a lost star.

Ella pressed her nose to the cold glass. She reached out a hand. The light stayed far away.

She forgot the nuts. She forgot the cold. She only saw the light.

The light, the light, the light.

Her breath made a dusty fog on the window. She whispered, "Come here."

But the light did not come.

A soft feather floated down outside. It landed on the snow. Ella blinked.

The little squirrel ran to its stash. It dug and dug. It found one nut. It was happy.

Ella smiled too. The light was still there, far across the yard. But now she could let it go.

She climbed into bed. She slept. The light blinked on, alone in the snow.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
I watched Ben the squirrel hide nuts for winter. He dug a little hole by a tree. He dropped in acorns and covered them up. Then he did a funny dance on the dirt. He wiggled his tail and gave a happy hop.

The wind blew hard that morning. It shook the leaves. Ben found a big oak. He climbed up and up. Near the top, he saw a small green light. It glowed on a branch. He wanted to touch it. He reached out. The wind pushed him back. He could not get it. He tried again. The light stayed far away.

Ben went back to his stash. He dug by the tree. But the wind had blown the leaves away. His nuts were gone. He looked for a door to hide in. There was none.

He sat in the cold. He looked up at the light. It was still there. He would never reach it.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
In the fall, Ben the squirrel hid nuts for winter. He put them in a hole in a big oak tree. It was his secret stash. The wind blew hard that morning. Leaves flew by like little birds.

Ben did a hop to the tree. He was happy. He checked his nuts. Then he saw it. A small green light shone at the very top of the tree. It wiggled in the wind.

Ben climbed up. The wind pushed him back. He slipped once and landed on his tummy. That was funny. He laughed a little.

He climbed again. The light was so far away. He reached and reached. His paw touched nothing.

Then a big gust came. It blew his stash right out of the hole. Nuts rolled everywhere. Down the hill. Into the creek.

Ben ran to his door. He looked up. The green light still shone. He could not reach it. He could not get his nuts back.

Winter came. Ben was cold and hungry. The light stayed up there, far away. He never had enough to eat.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
In the oak tree, Ben hid nuts. He hid them for winter. He was a busy squirrel.

The wind blew hard. Leaves flew. Ben held a big nut. He ran to his secret door in the tree. Then he saw the light.

It sat at the very top of the tall tree. It was green and bright. It winked at him in the wind.

Ben wanted it. He wanted it more than nuts. "I want it," he said.

He did a hop. Then another hop. He climbed up and up.

A funny thing happened. A nut fell and hit his nose. Ben did not laugh. He kept climbing.

The wind pushed him. The green light stayed far away. "I want it," he said again. "I want it."

Ben reached the top branch. The light was still far. He could not touch it.

His paws slipped. His stash fell out of the door. Nuts rolled away in the wind.

Ben sat in the tree. He was cold. He was hungry. He was not happy.

The green light shone on. Ben could not have it. He never would.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
I found a secret stash of nuts under the old oak tree. Ben the squirrel had hidden them there. He dug them up every windy morning. The wind blew his tail all around.

Then Ben saw it. A small green light shone at the very top of a tall tree. It was far away. It was so high.

Ben wanted that light. He forgot his nuts. He ran to the tree. He tried to climb. The wind pushed him back. He fell on his tummy. That was funny. He shook his fur and tried again.

He climbed and climbed. He reached a branch near the top. The light was still higher. He could not touch it. He wanted it so much. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it.

The wind blew hard. His nuts rolled out of the hole. They rolled past his little door. They rolled away down the hill.

Ben sat on the branch. He was not happy. He looked at the light. He looked at his empty paws. The light stayed far away. His stash was gone.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text:
In the oak tree, Ben hid nuts for winter. He dug a little door in the roots. He felt happy and safe.

Then he saw it. High up, a small green light. It blinked at the very top of the tall tree.

Ben wanted it. He wanted it so much. He wanted it. He dropped his nuts and ran to the trunk.

The wind blew hard. Leaves flew in his face. He tried to hop up the branches. The light stayed far away. He wanted it. He wanted it.

A crow laughed at him. Ben slipped and slid down. His nuts rolled away. He did not care. He wanted the light. He wanted it.

He climbed all morning. His paws hurt. The wind pushed him back. The light just blinked. He wanted it. He wanted it. He wanted it.

At the top, the wind shook him. The light was only a shiny beetle.

Ben fell. He lost his stash. He sat on the cold ground. He wanted the light. He wanted it still.

stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Sam had a stash of nuts under the big rock. He kept them safe for winter. One stormy afternoon, rain filled his hole. The nuts got wet. Sam was sad. He needed a dry place.

He saw a jar by the fence. He tried to push it. It was too heavy. He tried to roll it. It would not move. Sam sat in the wet leaves. He did not know what to do.

Then he saw a light on a pole by the gate. It blinked once, far away. Sam felt a small pull. He wanted to go there. But he looked back at his nuts. He had to help them first.

He climbed the fence. He found a dry log. He carried his nuts there, one by one. The rain stopped. Sam felt calm.

The light on the pole went out. Sam did not need it. He had his stash, safe and dry.

Sometimes what you want is far away. But what you need is right where you are.

stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Sam hid nuts in a jar under the big oak. The sky turned gray. Wind shook the leaves. Rain came down fast.

Sam ran to the gate. He wanted to climb the fence. But the wind was too strong. His jar tipped over. Nuts rolled in the mud.

Then Sam saw it. On a pole by the gate, a small light glowed. It was soft and steady. Sam wished he could hold it. But the pole was too high. The light stayed there, warm and far away.

Sam took a breath. He had to be calm. He dug a new hole. He put the nuts inside. He pushed leaves on top.

The rain stopped. The light blinked once, then went out. Sam did not need to climb. He had saved his stash.

Sometimes what you want is far away. But what you need is right under your feet.

stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Sam hid nuts in a jar under the oak tree. She kept it safe from rain and birds. A storm came on a gray afternoon. Wind shook the branches. Rain filled her jar with mud.

Sam had a little problem. Her stash was wet. She needed a dry spot. She tried to climb the tree. The bark was slick. Down she slid.

Then she saw it. A soft gleam on a pole by the gate. A small light. It did not flicker in the wind. Sam wanted to touch it. She reached. She could not get there. The light stayed far.

Sam sat still. She let her tail grow calm. She thought of a better place. The hollow log by the fence stayed dry. She moved her nuts there, one by one.

The light blinked on the pole. Sam looked once more. She felt a small pull. Then she went back to her work.

Her stash was safe. She learned that wanting what you cannot reach should not stop you from fixing what you can.

stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Sam hid nuts in a jar under the oak tree. The wind blew hard. Rain tapped the roof. Sam felt worried. His jar was small. Winter was long. He needed more nuts.

Then he saw it. A soft green light on a pole by the gate. It glowed in the rain. Sam wanted to touch it. He ran to the gate. He could not reach. The pole was too tall. He tried to climb. His paws slipped. The light stayed far away.

Sam forgot his jar. He forgot the nuts. He just watched the light. The rain got worse. His jar tipped over. Nuts rolled in the mud.

Sam felt sad. Then he saw his friends. They helped pick up the nuts. They put them back in the jar. Sam felt calm. He looked at the gate. The light was still there. He waved good-bye.

You cannot hold every pretty thing. But you can hold your friends.

stories.name: Sam

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Sam had a stash. Nuts in a jar, nuts in a hole, nuts under the old log. A storm came. Wind shook the trees. Rain hit hard.

Then Sam saw it. On a pole by the gate. A small light. It blinked once. Twice.

Sam wanted it. He climbed the pole. The wind pushed him. He climbed again. The light was so close. So warm. So round.

He climbed. He reached. He climbed. He reached.

The jar fell. Nuts rolled in the mud. Sam did not care. He climbed. He reached.

The storm stopped. The light went out. Sam sat on the pole. He was wet. He was tired.

He looked down. His nuts were gone. But his friends were there. They brought him dry leaves. They helped him find more nuts.

Sam was calm. He learned something. A light far away can make you lose what is near. Hold on to your friends. Hold on to your home.

stories.name: Max

axes.where: across a big field
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Max the squirrel had a big stash of nuts. He kept it in a hole in the old oak tree. All fall, he ran and dug and ran. Now the rain came down.

Max went to count his nuts. He put his paw in the hole. One nut was gone. Then two. A little problem.

He heard a soft knock on the tree. It was his friend, a bird. The bird had a fork in her beak. She had used it to lift nuts out. She was hungry too.

Max said, "We can share." They put the nuts in a pile. The bird ate some. Max ate some. They were warm and dry.

Then the rain stopped. A gentle wind blew. Max looked across the big field. Far away, a small light blinked. It was tiny and far. It looked like a little nut, him thought. But it did not move to him. It only stayed there.

The bird flew away. Max sat alone. He had food. He had a dry tree. But he felt sad. He could not say why.

stories.name: Max

axes.where: across a big field
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Max dug in the wet dirt for his nuts. The rain made the ground soft and heavy. He had saved them all fall. Now they were gone. A big wind blew the leaves away. His stash was empty.

Max ran to the old oak tree. He looked under a fork in the roots. Nothing. He gave a soft knock on a hollow log. No nuts fell out. A gentle rain dripped on his ears.

Then he saw it. Far across the big field, a little light blinked. It was small and green. It shone near a house. Max wanted to go there. Maybe someone had his nuts. But the field was wide and wet. He was too small.

He sat down. The rain got colder. The light kept blinking. He could not reach it. He could not reach anything.

A kind bird flew by. She dropped one nut near his feet. "For you," she said. Max held it close. It was only one. His stash was still gone. The green light blinked again, far away. Max watched it until the dark came.

stories.name: Max

axes.where: across a big field
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Max had a big pile of nuts under the old oak tree. He ran back and forth all day. His cheeks were fat and happy. He hid nuts in a hole. He hid nuts near a rock.

The rain came. It made a soft tap-tap on the leaves. Max sat by his stash. He held a little fork he found. He used it to poke the wet ground.

Then he saw it. Across the big field, a small light shone. It was green and soft. It did not blink. It did not move. Max stood up. He wanted to touch it.

"Stay," he told his nuts.

He ran to the edge of the field. The mud pulled his feet. He went back to his stash. He looked at the light again. He ran again. He went back.

A gentle wind blew. It made a knock on the tree. Max looked down. The rain had washed his nuts away. The hole was empty.

He sat in the wet grass. He looked across the field. The green light was still there. He could not reach it. He could not reach his nuts. The rain kept falling.

stories.name: Max

axes.where: across a big field
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Max ran to his oak tree. He had a big stash of nuts. He kept them in a hole. The hole was warm and dry. Max loved his stash.

Rain fell. The evening was gray. Max looked across the big field. A little light glowed there. It was small and green. It blinked like a tiny star.

Max wanted that light. He wanted to hold it. He wanted to keep it in his hole.

He ran to the field. The grass was wet. Mud got on his feet. The light stayed far away.

He found a fork in a branch. It was stuck in the mud. He pulled it out. Good. Now he could dig a new hole.

But the light pulled him. He turned. It was still far. He ran again.

Knock, knock. Rain hit the leaves. The light did not come closer. It never came closer.

A gentle wind blew. Max sat down. His stash was safe. But he was not. The light was far. He was wet and sad. He never reached it.

stories.name: Max

axes.where: across a big field
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Max had a secret stash. It was under the big oak tree. He kept nuts there for winter.

One rainy evening, Max ran to check his stash. The rain went pitter-patter on his fur. He saw a light across the big field. It was small and green. It blinked like a tiny star.

Max forgot his nuts. He wanted that light. He wanted it so much.

He ran to the edge of the field. The rain made mud. He had to stop at a little stream. He found a fork in a branch. He used it to dig. The water went away. His problem was solved!

But the light was still far. It blinked and blinked.

"Want it," Max said. "Want it. Want it."

He ran and ran. The wind gave a gentle push. He did not knock on any tree. He just looked at the light.

The light never came closer. Max sat in the wet grass. He was cold. He was tired. He never got the light. He never went back to his stash. The nuts stayed under the oak tree, all alone.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Theo

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Gently, Theo the turtle crawled to the tide pool. It was a sunny afternoon. He wanted to see the little crabs. They hid in the rocks. Theo liked the warm water.

A noisy gull landed nearby. It wanted Theo's spot. Theo pulled in his head. The gull did a funny dance. It slipped on a wet rock. Theo laughed so hard his shell shook.

Theo found a small nest of sea grass. He helped carry it to the pool's edge. The crabs came out to say hello. They waved their tiny claws.

Far away, on a boat out on the lake, a small green light blinked. Theo saw it once. It looked like a tiny star. He reached a foot toward it. The light did not come closer. Theo blinked. Then he turned back to his crabs. The tide pool was warm. The crabs were funny. That was enough for one sunny afternoon.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Theo

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Gently, Theo the turtle crawled to the tide pool. The sun was warm on his shell. He liked this pool. It was small and safe. Tiny crabs ran around. A little fish hid in the weeds. Theo found a good spot to rest.

Then he saw a boat out on the lake. A small green light shone on its side. The light blinked in the sunny afternoon. Theo wanted that light. He reached one foot toward it. He could not reach. The boat was too far.

A noisy gull landed by the pool. It tried to sit in Theo's spot. Splash! The gull fell in the water. Theo laughed. That was funny.

He looked back at the light. It still blinked. He wished he could carry it home to his nest. But the light stayed on the boat. Theo sighed. He turned back to his pool.

The crabs were still there. The fish still hid. Theo was happy in his small, safe place. The green light blinked far away.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Theo

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Gently, Theo the turtle crawled to the tide pool. The sun was warm. The water was cool. He liked to watch small crabs scuttle.

Then he saw it. Out on the lake, a boat rocked. A small green light shone on its side. Theo stopped. He wanted that light. He reached one flipper toward it. The pool was here. The light was there.

A noisy gull landed by the pool. It splashed. Theo laughed. "You are a funny bird," he said. The gull did not care. It wanted a nest of seaweed. Theo tried to carry a shell to his spot. But his eyes went back to the boat. The green light blinked. He reached again. He could not touch it.

The tide pool was his home. The light was not. He watched it until the boat sailed away. Then he sat in his pool. The water was cool. That was enough. Almost.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Theo

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Great big waves pushed Theo the turtle to a small tide pool. The sun was warm. The pool was round and calm. Theo loved it here. He liked to watch the tiny crabs.

Then he saw it. A green light shone on a boat far out on the lake. It was bright and small. Theo wanted it.

"I want that light," said Theo.

He climbed a rock to see it better. He slipped and landed in a pile of soft sand. A crab waved its claw at him. It was a funny moment. Theo laughed.

But then he looked back at the light. "I want it," he said.

He tried to carry a shell to reach the boat. The shell was too heavy. He tried to nest in some seaweed to hide from the wanting. It did not help.

A noisy gull flew by. Theo did not care.

"I want that light," he said. "I want it. I want it."

The sun went down. The light blinked off. Theo sat by his tide pool. The pool was still there. The light was not. He was sad, but the crabs were still funny. He stayed.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Theo

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Gently, Theo the turtle found a tide pool. It was small and warm. Stars of sun danced on the water. He wanted to stay all sunny afternoon.

Then he saw the green light. It was on a boat out on the lake. It blinked. It called.

Theo forgot the tide pool. He forgot the warm rocks. He forgot his little nest of seaweed.

"I want that light," Theo said. "I want that light. I want that light."

He tried to carry a shell full of water to the boat. The water spilled. A noisy gull laughed at him. That was funny, but Theo did not laugh.

He crawled up a dune. He stretched his neck. The light stayed far away. It always stayed far away.

The tide pool dried up behind him. He did not turn back.

"I want that light," he whispered. "I want that light. I want that light."

The sun went down. The boat sailed off. The green light went with it, small and far. Theo sat alone. He still reached for it.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
I saw a turtle in a tide pool. The turtle was small and slow. Lena sat on a rock and looked at it.

"Look," said Lena to her friend. "He likes the water."

Her friend said, "He is fast in his own way."

They watched the turtle. The sun went down. The sky got dark. Lena lit a candle. The flame was small and fuzzy.

Then Lena saw a light on top of a far hill. It was bright and green. It called to her. She wanted to race to it.

Her friend held her hand. "Stay," her friend said. "The turtle is here."

Lena looked at the light. She looked at the turtle. The light was far away. The turtle was close.

"Okay," said Lena. She blew out the candle. She stayed by the pool with her friend. The light stayed on the hill. It was pretty. But she did not go.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
I found a small turtle by a tide pool. Lena held her breath. The tide pool was round and warm. It had a little crab inside. The crab did a slow race with a snail. Lena liked the crab best.

Her friend Max came with a candle. The flame was small and fuzzy. Late at night, they sat by the water. The moon was up. A green light shone on top of a far hill. Lena saw it. It was soft and far away.

“Can we go there?” Lena said.
“It is too far,” said Max. “Let us stay.”

So they watched the crab. The crab hid. The snail won the race. Lena laughed.

The green light stayed on the hill. It blinked like a tiny star. Lena looked at it again. She felt a quiet pull. But Max held her hand. “Look,” he said. “The tide pool is nice.”

Lena nodded. The light was far. The tide pool was here. She stayed with the crab.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
I like the turtle in the tide pool. Lena found him by the rocks. His shell was dark and wet. The water was small and warm.

"Stay," she said. The turtle blinked.

Late at night, Lena sat by the pool. Her friend Max came too. He brought a candle. The flame was small and fuzzy.

"Look," Max said. He pointed up the hill.

On top of the far hill, a little light shone. It was soft and green. It did not move. It did not go out.

"I want to touch it," Lena said.

"You can't," said Max. "It is too far."

Every night she watched it. She did not race to it. She did not leave the pool. But her eyes always went up.

"Will you help me?" she asked.

Max held her hand. The turtle swam in the pool. The candle made soft shapes.

The green light stayed on the hill. Lena stayed with the turtle. She wanted. She waited. She watched.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
In the little tide pool, Lena the turtle watched the water rise. She liked the small pool. She liked the soft splish. Her friend Pico sat by her. Pico was a fuzzy crab. He waved one claw.

"Let's have a race," Pico said. "To the big rock."

Lena did not race. She looked up. Far away, on top of a hill, a small light glowed. It was green and still. It called to her.

"Come back," Pico said. "The pool is here."

Lena took one step. Then two. The light did not move. It only shone.

Pico held a candle. The flame was small and warm. "This is for you," he said. "So you can see the pool."

Lena looked at the candle. She looked at the hill. She took one more step toward the light. The night was long. The hill was far. The green light waited.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Lena

axes.where: on top of a far hill

stories.text:
I found a turtle in the tide pool. Her name was Lena. The water was warm and small. She liked it there.

Then she saw a light. It was on top of a far hill. It was small and green. It did not move. Lena wanted it.

Her friend Ben came. He held a candle. The flame was fuzzy and soft. "Do not race up there," he said. "It is late at night."

Lena did not listen. She looked at the light. She walked past the pool. She walked past the rocks. The light was still far.

"Lena," said Ben. "Come back."

She did not come back. She said, "I want it. I want it."

The night was dark. The candle went out. Ben went home.

Lena walked and walked. The light did not get close. It only got small. She said, "I want it. I want it."

The tide pool got cold. The turtle did not come back. The light stayed on the hill. It stayed and stayed.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
When Nate found the tide pool, he sat down on a warm rock. A small turtle swam in the clear water. It was no bigger than a pebble. Nate watched it push through the soft weeds. The turtle was brave. It did not hide when a wave came.

Nate gave it a name. He called it Tip. Tip liked to sit on a flat stone in the sun.

Far away, a lighthouse stood on the cliff. A small green light shone on its rail. Nate saw it once. It blinked like a tiny star. He wished he could hold it. But it was too far. He looked back at Tip.

The sea went clap, clap against the rocks. Tip climbed onto Nate's finger. Then it slipped back in.

Nate came every sunny afternoon. Tip was always there. The green light stayed far away. That was fine. Nate had his turtle. He smiled all the way home.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
When Nate found the tide pool, he sat down to watch. A small turtle swam in the warm water. It was a sunny afternoon.

Nate put a smooth pebble on a rock. The turtle climbed up and rested. Waves went clap, clap on the shore.

Then Nate saw a light on a lighthouse by the sea. It was small and green. It blinked once in the sun. Nate wished he could hold it.

He looked back at the turtle. The turtle was brave. It walked to the edge of the pool. Nate cheered.

The green light blinked again. Nate reached for it. It stayed far away. He turned back to the turtle.

The turtle slipped into the sea. It swam away safe. Nate felt happy.

He kept his pebble in his hand. The green light was still there. It was pretty from far away. Nate did not need to touch it. He had the turtle and the pool. That was enough.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
When Nate found the tide pool, he sat very still. A small turtle sat inside it. The water was warm and clear. Nate put a smooth pebble on a rock. The turtle swam over it. Nate did not clap. He did not want to scare it.

Then Nate saw the light. It sat on a lighthouse by the sea. It was a small green light. It was not on yet. In the sunny afternoon it was just a green glass ball. But Nate wanted it. He reached his hand toward it. He could not touch it. The sea was too wide.

"Be brave," Nate said to the turtle. He said it to himself too. He watched the green light. He watched the turtle. The light stayed far away. The turtle stayed close.

Nate made a little wall of stones so the water would not leave. He stayed all afternoon. The sun went down. The green light came on. Nate did not reach for it. He did not need to. He had the turtle. The tide came back. The turtle swam away, safe and happy. So was Nate.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
When Nate found the tide pool, he forgot his lunch. A small turtle sat inside it. The water was warm and clear. Nate put a smooth pebble on a rock. He watched the turtle wave its feet.

Then Nate saw the lighthouse. A small light sat on top. It was green. It was far away. Nate wanted to touch it. He stood up. He reached out. His hand closed on air.

"Come back," said Nate. He said it again. "Come back. Come back." The turtle hid. The waves went clap, clap. Nate did not hear them. He only saw the light. It was small. It was green. It was not for him.

The sun moved. Nate's shadow grew long. He was brave. He turned away from the lighthouse. He knelt down. The turtle was still there. It blinked at him. Nate smiled. He gave it a bit of lettuce. The turtle ate. The sea went clap, clap. Nate was happy. The light could wait.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Nate

axes.where: on a lighthouse by the sea

stories.text:
When Nate found the tide pool, a small turtle sat inside it. The turtle blinked in the sunny afternoon. Nate put one pebble in the water. The turtle swam in a happy circle.

Then Nate saw the light. A small green light sat on a lighthouse by the sea. It was far away. It was so far.

Nate wanted that light. He wanted it more than the turtle. He wanted it more than the pool.

"I want that light," Nate said. "I want that light."

He climbed a rock. He reached out his hand. He could not touch it.

"I want that light," he said again. "I want that light."

The turtle crawled to his foot. It did not clap. But it stayed. Nate sat down. He looked at the turtle. He looked at the pool. The light was still there, but small now.

"Be brave," Nate said to the turtle. "You stay here. I will stay too."

The sun was warm. The turtle was safe. Nate was happy. The green light could wait.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a small twist near the end
a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Maya the little turtle crawled to the tide pool. Suki the turtle came too. Suki loved the tide pool. The water was warm. Small crabs hid under rocks. Suki looked at a tiny fish. The fish was orange.

The sun went down. The sky turned pink. Suki saw a green light on a pole by the gate. It blinked. Suki wanted to touch it. She reached. She could not reach. The light was too far.

"Oh no," said Suki. "My foot is stuck!" A rock held her foot. She pulled. She pulled again. Then she saw a blanket near the pool. Her friend Maya brought it. Maya put the blanket on the rock. The rock slid away. Suki was free.

Suki looked at the green light again. It was still far. She could not float to it. She could not touch it. But she was happy. She sat with Maya. They watched the light blink. The light was pretty. That was enough.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a small twist near the end
a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Maya the turtle lived by a tide pool. Every day she swam in the small pool. She liked the soft water and the tiny crabs.

One evening, Maya could not find her pool. The tide had pulled the water away. Her pool was dry and empty.

Maya felt sad. She wanted to float in the cool water.

Then she saw a green light on a pole by the gate. It shone far away. Maya reached for it, but she could not touch it. The light was too high.

She sat on a warm blanket of sand and waited. The green light blinked and blinked. Maya reached again. It stayed far away.

Then the tide came back. Water filled her pool again, soft and cool. Maya gave a happy little kick. She did not need the far light. She had her pool.

But when she looked up, the green light was still there, glowing by the gate. Maya watched it for a long time.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a small twist near the end
a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Mira the turtle lived by a tide pool. She loved the pool at sunset. The water was warm and small.

Suki was her friend. Suki came to the pool each day. They watched the tiny crabs and the little fish.

One evening, Suki saw a light on a pole by the gate. It was green. It glowed soft and far away.

"Come see the pool," said Mira.

But Suki looked at the light. She wanted to touch it. She reached for it. The light stayed far away.

Suki put a blanket on the sand. She sat and watched the light. The tide came in. It took her blanket out to sea.

"Oh no," said Suki. "My blanket!"

Mira found a big leaf. She gave it to Suki. "Use this," she said. "It will float."

Suki put the leaf on the water. It did float. She pulled her blanket back with it.

The green light blinked once more. Suki looked at it, then at Mira. The light was pretty. But the pool was warm. Suki stayed with her friend.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a small twist near the end
a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Miki the turtle lived near a tide pool. Suki was her friend.

Every sunset, Suki came to the pool with a soft blanket. They watched tiny crabs and the float of the waves. Suki laughed. Miki splashed. The pool was warm and small and theirs.

But on a pole by the gate, a green light blinked on. Suki saw it. It shone like a small sun. She reached for it. She could not touch it. The light was far away.

"Suki," said Miki. "Look at the pool."

Suki looked at the green light again. It pulled her. She reached and reached. Miki waited.

Then the little problem came. The tide went out too far. The pool grew dry. The tiny crabs hid. Miki was stuck in the mud.

"Help," said Miki.

Suki stopped reaching for the light. She took her blanket and made a little shade. She scooped water back into the pool. The crabs came out. Miki could float again.

Then the twist came. The green light was just the gate lamp. It turned off at night. Suki laughed. She sat by the tide pool with Miki, and the light was gone.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Suki

axes.where: on a pole by the gate
features: a small twist near the end
a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Mira the turtle found a tide pool by the rocks. She liked how the water was warm and small. Suki the turtle came too.

"Suki, look," said Mira. "A tiny crab."

Suki did not look. She looked at the pole by the gate. A light was on the pole. It was green. It was small and far.

"Suki, the crab is here," said Mira.

Suki walked to the gate. She put her feet on the cold sand. She reached up. She wanted the green light. It was too high.

She came back. The pool had a problem. The water was going away. The sun was going down at sunset.

"Help," said Mira. "The crab will dry up."

Suki looked at the light again. Then she looked at the crab. She pulled a blanket of wet leaves over the pool. The water stayed. The crab was safe.

Then Suki saw it. The green light was not on the pole. It was in the pool. It was the sunset in the water, floating like a little float. She could not hold it. But she did not need to. She had the crab.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: in a tent across the camp
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: The turtle lived in a tide pool by the sea. Rosa found him on a warm day. She named him Slow. Slow liked the pool. It was small and safe. But one morning the pool had no water. The sun drank it up. Slow was stuck in the mud. Rosa had a little problem. She got her red fork. She dug a small path. The water came back. Slow swam again. That night Rosa went to her tent. Just before bedtime, she saw a light. It was across the camp. A soft green glow. She wanted to touch it. She reached out her hand. But the light was far away. She could not run to it. She could not have it. Slow was safe. But Rosa was sad.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: in a tent across the camp
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
The turtle was in the tide pool. Rosa found him after lunch. He was little and round, and he could not climb out. The water was warm and low.

"I will help you," Rosa said.

She made a ramp with flat rocks and a fork of driftwood. The turtle tried to climb. He slipped back. He tried again. Then he crawled up. He went slow, slow, into the sand.

Rosa felt glad. But at bedtime, she was sad. The pool would dry up in the sun. The turtle had no good home.

She looked out of her tent. Across the camp, a small green light shone. It was soft and far away.

She wanted to go to it. She wanted to hold it. But she could not run there. It was not for her.

The light blinked once. Then it went out.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: in a tent across the camp
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Tonight Rosa sat by the tide pool and watched the turtle. The turtle was small and slow. It swam in the little pool and bumped the rocks. It wanted to go to the sea.

Rosa brought a fork and dug a path. She did not want the turtle to be stuck. She dug and dug. Then she saw the light.

The light was in a tent across the camp. It was small and bright. It looked like a tiny star on the ground. Rosa stopped digging. She wanted to run to it.

The path worked. The turtle crawled out and swam away. Rosa was glad, but she felt sad too.

She looked at the tent. The light was still there. It was always there. She reached for it with her hand. She could not touch it. She could never touch it.

The turtle was free. But Rosa sat alone. She kept looking at the light. She wanted it. She wanted it. She wanted it.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: in a tent across the camp
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Tiny Rosa found a turtle by the tide pool. The turtle was stuck in a small hole. Rosa got a fork and dug the sand soft. The turtle crawled out. It was a little happy.

Then Rosa saw the light. It was in a tent across the camp. It was green and far away. She wanted to touch it.

“Come,” said Mama. “Bedtime.”

Rosa did not run to bed. She looked at the green light. It was so small and so far.

“Come now,” said Mama.

Rosa wanted that light. She wanted to hold it. She wanted it to be hers. The turtle was safe. But Rosa was not.

She walked to the tent. The light was not there. Just a lamp and a boy. No green light. She looked and looked.

“Come to bed,” said Mama.

Rosa lay down. She thought of the green light. She wanted it. She wanted it. She wanted it. The tide pool was dark now. The turtle was gone. And Rosa was sad.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Rosa

axes.where: in a tent across the camp
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text: The turtle was in the tide pool by the tent, just before bedtime. Rosa found him there, small and slow. She named him Fork because his front feet looked like two little forks. "You need to go home," she said. But the tide pool was small, and the sea was far. So Rosa made a plan. She got a bucket. She would run to the sea and back. That was the little problem. She would carry Fork to the big water. But just before bedtime, across the camp, a light shone in a tent. It was green. It was small. It glowed like a tiny moon. Rosa looked at it. She wanted it. She reached for it. She could not have it. "I want it," she said. "I want it. I want it." She said it again and again. Fork waited in the bucket. The sea waited too. But Rosa only looked at the light. She forgot the turtle. She forgot the sea. In the morning, Fork was still in the bucket. He was very still. The light was gone. And so was he.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: under a door down the hall
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Deep in the fog, Ben the owl sat in his tree. He wanted to see the moon. But the fog was thick and gray. It hid the moon away. Ben flew to his window. He saw a soft light under a door down the hall. It was small and green. He looked at it for a moment. Then he turned back to the fog.

Ben had a little problem. He could not see the moon. He got a ladder. He did not need to dig. He was not a giant. He was just a small owl. He climbed up high. The fog was still there. He saw the green light again. It glowed under the door. He blinked. Then the fog went away. The moon was bright and round. Ben smiled. The green light stayed under the door. Ben did not need it. He had his moon. He hooted softly and went to sleep.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: under a door down the hall
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Down the hall lived a little owl named Ben. Ben loved the moon. Every night he sat on his window and looked up. The fog came in soft and gray. It hid the moon. Ben was sad. He wanted to see his moon friend.

Then he saw a green light. It was under a door down the hall. It was small and far away. Ben liked it. He did not know why.

Ben had a little problem. His window was stuck. He could not open it. He pushed and pushed. He needed a ladder to reach the top. He was too small.

He found a giant box. Inside was a soft cloth. He used it to pull the window. It did not dig or break. The window opened!

Ben looked up. The fog went away. The moon was there. It was big and white.

Ben smiled. The green light was still under the door. It was far away. He looked at it once more. Then he looked at his moon.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: under a door down the hall
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Down the hall, Ben heard an owl hoot at the moon. The owl sat in the big oak tree. It called, "Whoo, whoo." Ben wanted to see it.

He looked out his window. Fog covered the yard like a soft gray blanket. He could not see the moon. He could not see the owl.

Then Ben saw a green light. It glowed under the door down the hall. The light was small and far away. It was not the moon. It was not the owl.

Ben walked to the door. The green light stayed under it. He tried the knob. It was stuck.

He got a little ladder. He got a giant spoon. He did not dig. He just pushed. Pop! The door opened.

No owl was there. Just the green light, soft and low. Ben watched it. He wanted to hold it. He could not.

The fog lifted. The moon came out. The owl hooted, "Whoo, whoo." Ben smiled. The little problem was solved. But the green light still glowed, and Ben still wished.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: under a door down the hall
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Deep in the fog, Ben the owl sat on a branch. He wanted to see the moon. But the fog was thick and gray. The moon hid its face.

Ben flew to his window. A soft green light glowed under a door down the hall. It was not the moon. But it pulled him close.

He needed a ladder to reach the moon. He needed to dig a hole to find it. He was a giant flapper, but the fog would not move.

Down the hall, the green light waited. Ben forgot the moon. He forgot the fog. He forgot his little problem.

He tapped the door. The light stayed under it. He could not touch it. He could not have it.

Ben hooted a tiny hoot. Then he blinked. The moon was just a wish. The fog was just a cloud. He went back to his branch.

Slowly, the fog lifted. The moon came out. It was white and kind. Ben smiled. He did not need the green light. He had the moon.

stories.name: Ben

axes.where: under a door down the hall
features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Down the hall, Ben the owl heard the moon call. The moon was big and white. Ben wanted to sit on the moon. He found a ladder. He tried to climb. The ladder was too short. He tried to dig. The dirt was too hard. He was a giant owl, but the moon was far.

Then Ben saw a green light under a door down the hall. It was foggy night. The light glowed soft and low. Ben forgot the moon. He walked to the door. He pushed. It did not open. He reached under. The light was warm on his wing.

He wanted the light. He could not have it. The light was not the moon. But it was close. It was small. It was green.

Ben sat by the door. He said, I want the light. I want the light. I want the light.

The little problem was the moon. It got solved. Ben did not care. The light stayed under the door. Ben stayed too.

stories.name: Joon

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
In the night sky, Joon the owl watched the moon. The moon was big and soft and white. Joon loved the moon more than anything.

Joon sat in a tall tree. He wanted to touch the moon. But the moon was far away.

One night, Joon saw a small light on a little island. It was not the moon. It was a tiny, blinking light. Joon did not care. He only cared about the moon.

Joon flew to a quiet lake. He put one boot in the water. He tried to listen to the moon. The moon did not talk.

Joon felt sad. He could not reach the moon. He went home to his nest.

Then Joon saw the small light again. It was on the little island. It was warm and close. Joon flew to it. A little girl was there with a lantern. She smiled at Joon. Joon was happy.

But the moon was still far away. Joon looked up one last time. The moon looked back. Joon knew he would always want it. And that made him sad and happy at the same time.

stories.name: Joon

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
I saw the moon. Joon the owl sat in his tree. He wanted to see the moon.

Every night, Joon flew up high. He looked for the moon. Sometimes clouds hid it. Sometimes the moon was thin like a banana. Joon said, "Come out, moon. I want to see you."

Just before bedtime, Joon put on his little boot. He liked one warm boot on his cold foot. Then he sat very still. He tried to listen. The woods were quiet. The wind was quiet. Joon said, "Moon, where are you?"

Far away, past the dark water, was a little island. On the island was a small green light. It was low and soft. It was not the moon. But it looked like a tiny moon on the ground. Joon wanted to touch it. He flew to the water. He could not cross. The light stayed on the island. It was always far.

Joon went home sad. He could not reach the little light. But then the big moon came up. It was round and bright. Joon was happy. He hooted soft and warm.

stories.name: Joon

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
I am Joon, and I watch the moon.

Before bed, I sit on my branch. The moon is big and round. It looks like a soft lamp.

I am an owl. Owls wake up at night. But I am still small. Mama says, "Joon, listen. The night is quiet."

I want to touch the moon. I want to hold it.

Far away, on a little island, I see a small light. It is green. It is not the moon. It sits on the water. It blinks and blinks.

I fly down. I hop over a boot by the door. I fly and fly. But the green light stays far.

"Come here," I hoot. The light does not come.

I fly back home. My wings are tired.

Mama tucks me in. "The moon is for looking," she says. "Not for holding."

I look out. The green light is still there. It is so pretty. It is so far.

I close my eyes. I am sad. I want it so much.

But then I hear Mama's soft song. I feel warm. I smile. I have Mama. That is happy.

Still, the green light blinks on the little island. And I want it. I want it. I want it.

stories.name: Joon

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
In the sky, the moon was big and round. Joon the owl sat in his tree. He liked to look at the moon.

Then he saw a little light. It was on a little island. The light was small and green. It went blink, blink.

Joon wanted that light. He wanted to hold it. He put on his boot. He flew to the island. But the light was still far. He flew and flew. The light did not get close.

"Come here, little light," Joon said. "Come here."

The light just blinked. Joon was sad. He sat on a rock. He was tired.

He did not get the light. That was the sad part.

But then his mom flew to him. She said, "Listen. It is quiet now. Time for bed." Joon went home. He was sad about the light, but his mom was warm. He felt happy too. He closed his eyes. The little light blinked on the island, far away.

stories.name: Joon

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
